bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第180卷卷第一百八十

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 180, juan number one hundred eighty.
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 180

sentences.zh: 【隋紀四】 起閼逢困敦，盡強圉單閼，凡四年。

translations.literal: [Sui Annals 4] From Eyu Kundun through Qiangyu Dan'e; four years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Sui Annals 4] From Eyu Kundun through Qiangyu Dan'e—four years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙午，赦天下。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day bingwu: amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first month, day bingwu, an amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 帝將避暑於仁壽宮，術士章仇太翼固諫；

translations.literal: The emperor was about to take the summer retreat at Renshou Palace; the technician Zhangqiu Taiyi firmly remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was preparing to spend the summer at Renshou Palace, and the diviner Zhangqiu Taiyi remonstrated with him at length.

sentences.zh: 不聽，太翼曰：「是行恐鑾輿不返！」

translations.literal: He did not listen. Taiyi said: "On this journey I fear the imperial carriage will not return!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not heed him. Taiyi said, "On this journey I fear Your Majesty's carriage will not return!"

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，系之長安獄，期還而斬之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged, imprisoned him in Chang'an jail, and set a date to behead him upon return.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, had him thrown into the Chang'an prison, and set a date to execute him when he returned.

sentences.zh: 甲子，幸仁壽宮。

translations.literal: Day jiazi: he visited Renshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On day jiazi he proceeded to Renshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，詔賞賜支度，事無鉅細，並付皇太子。

translations.literal: Day yichou: an edict that rewards and expenditures, matters great and small alike, were all entrusted to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On day yichou an edict ordered that all rewards and expenditures, whether great or small, be handled by the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙卯，帝不豫。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day yimao: the emperor was unwell.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on day yimao, the emperor fell ill.

sentences.zh: 六月，庚申，赦天下。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day gengshen: amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on day gengshen, an amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲辰，上疾甚，臥與百僚辭訣，並握手歔欷，命太子赦章仇太翼。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day jiachen: the emperor's illness was severe; lying down he bade farewell to the hundred officials, all grasping hands and weeping, and ordered the crown prince to pardon Zhangqiu Taiyi.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on day jiachen, the emperor's illness grew grave. Prostrate in bed he took leave of the officials, all grasping hands and weeping together, and commanded the crown prince to pardon Zhangqiu Taiyi.

sentences.zh: 丁未，崩於大寶殿。

translations.literal: Day dingwei: he died in the Dabao Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On day dingwei he died in the Dabao Hall.

sentences.zh: 高祖性嚴重，令行禁止，勤於政事。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu's nature was stern and grave; orders issued were forbidden to violate; he was diligent in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was stern and dignified; his orders were obeyed without exception, and he was tireless in governing.

sentences.zh: 每旦聽朝，日昃忘倦。

translations.literal: Each dawn he held court; when the sun slanted westward he forgot weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Each morning he held court, and when the sun had passed its zenith he still showed no sign of fatigue.

sentences.zh: 雖嗇於財，至於賞賜有功，即無所愛；

translations.literal: Although sparing with wealth, when it came to rewarding merit he held back nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Though he was frugal with money, when it came to rewarding merit he held nothing back.

sentences.zh: 將士戰沒，必加優賞，仍遣使者勞問其家。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers who died in battle invariably received generous rewards, and envoys were still sent to console their families.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers who fell in battle always received generous rewards, and envoys were dispatched to comfort their families.

sentences.zh: 愛養百姓，勸課農桑，輕徭薄賦。

translations.literal: He cherished and nurtured the common people, encouraged agriculture and sericulture, and lightened corvée and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for the people, encouraged farming and sericulture, and kept corvée labor and taxes light.

sentences.zh: 其自奉養，務為儉素，乘輿御物，故弊者隨令補用；

translations.literal: In his own maintenance he strove for frugality and simplicity; imperial carriages and regalia—when worn out he at once ordered them patched for reuse.
translations.idiomatic: In his own living he insisted on austerity; when carriages and imperial goods wore out he had them repaired for continued use.

sentences.zh: 自非享宴，所食不過一肉；

translations.literal: Unless at a feast, what he ate was no more than one kind of meat.
translations.idiomatic: Except at banquets his meals included no more than a single dish of meat.

sentences.zh: 後宮皆服浣濯之衣。

translations.literal: The inner palace all wore washed and mended garments.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in the inner palace wore washed and mended clothing.

sentences.zh: 天下化之，開皇、仁壽之間，丈夫率衣絹布，不服綾綺，裝帶不過銅鐵骨角，無金玉之飾。

translations.literal: All under Heaven were transformed by this; between the Kaihuang and Renshou eras, men generally wore silk and cloth, did not wear brocade and gauze, and belt ornaments were no more than copper, iron, bone, and horn—without gold and jade adornment.
translations.idiomatic: The empire followed his example: during the Kaihuang and Renshou reigns men commonly wore plain silk and cloth, shunned brocades and gauzes, and belt fittings were of copper, iron, bone, or horn—never gold or jade.

sentences.zh: 故衣食滋殖，倉庫盈溢。

translations.literal: Therefore food and clothing multiplied, and storehouses overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: Food and clothing grew abundant, and the granaries brimmed full.

sentences.zh: 受禪之初，民戶不滿四百萬，末年，逾八百九十萬，獨冀州已一百萬戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of receiving the abdication, registered households were fewer than four million; by his last years they exceeded eight million nine hundred thousand, and Jizhou alone already had one million households.
translations.idiomatic: When he first accepted the throne there were fewer than four million registered households; by his final years there were more than eight million nine hundred thousand, and Jizhou alone already counted one million.

sentences.zh: 然猜忌苛察，信受讒言，功臣故舊，無始終保全者；

translations.literal: Yet he was suspicious and harshly scrutinizing, believed slander, and among meritorious ministers and old associates none was preserved intact from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was suspicious and exacting, readily believed slander, and not one of his meritorious ministers or old companions was spared to the end.

sentences.zh: 乃至子弟，皆如仇敵，此其所短也。

translations.literal: Even down to his sons and younger brothers—all were like enemies; this was his shortcoming.
translations.idiomatic: Even his own sons and brothers he treated like foes—this was his failing.

sentences.zh: 初，文獻皇后既崩，宣華夫人陳氏、容華夫人察氏皆有寵。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Empress Wenxian had died, Lady Xuanhua Chen and Lady Ronghua Cai both had favor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Empress Wenxian's death, Lady Xuanhua of the Chen clan and Lady Ronghua of the Cai clan had both won the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 陳氏，陳高宗之女；

translations.literal: The Chen clan—daughter of Chen Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chen was a daughter of Emperor Gao of Chen.

sentences.zh: 蔡氏，丹楊人也。

translations.literal: The Cai clan—a native of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cai was a native of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 上寢疾於仁壽宮，尚書左僕射楊素、兵部尚書柳述、黃門侍郎元巖皆入閣侍疾，召皇太子入居大寶殿。

translations.literal: The emperor lay ill at Renshou Palace; Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Yang Su, Minister of War Liu Shu, and Yellow Gate Attendant Yuan Yan all entered the inner chambers to attend the illness, and summoned the crown prince to reside in the Dabao Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill at Renshou Palace, Yang Su, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Liu Shu, Minister of War, and Yuan Yan, Yellow Gate Attendant, all entered the inner chambers to attend him, and the crown prince was summoned to take up residence in the Dabao Hall.

sentences.zh: 太子慮上有不諱，須預防擬，手自為書，封出問素；

translations.literal: The crown prince, fearing the emperor might suffer the unmentionable, needed to prepare preventive measures; he personally wrote a letter, sealed it, and sent it out to ask Su.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince, fearing the worst for his father, made advance preparations: he wrote a letter in his own hand, sealed it, and sent it to Yang Su for advice.

sentences.zh: 素條錄事狀以報太子。

translations.literal: Su itemized the circumstances in a report to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su drew up a detailed report of the situation and sent it to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 宮人誤送上所，上覽而大恚。

translations.literal: A palace woman mistakenly delivered it to the emperor's quarters; the emperor read it and was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: A palace woman mistakenly delivered the letter to the emperor instead; when he read it he was furious.

sentences.zh: 陳夫人平旦出更衣，為太子所逼，拒之，得免，歸於上所；

translations.literal: Lady Chen at daybreak went out to change clothes and was pressed by the crown prince; she resisted and escaped, and returned to the emperor's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Lady Chen went out to change her clothes and was accosted by the crown prince; she resisted him and got away, then hurried back to the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 上怪其神色有異，問其故。

translations.literal: The emperor wondered at her altered expression and asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noticed her distraught look and asked what had happened.

sentences.zh: 夫人泫然曰：「太子無禮！」

translations.literal: The lady said with tears: "The crown prince was disrespectful!"
translations.idiomatic: With tears in her eyes she said, "The crown prince behaved disgracefully toward me!"

sentences.zh: 上恚，抵床曰：「畜生何足付大事！

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged, struck the bed, and said: "That beast is not fit to be entrusted with great affairs!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged, struck the bed, and cried, "That brute is not fit to receive the great charge!

sentences.zh: 獨孤誤我！」

translations.literal: Dugu misled me!"
translations.idiomatic: Dugu misled me!"

sentences.zh: 乃呼柳述、元巖曰：「召我兒！」

translations.literal: He then called Liu Shu and Yuan Yan and said: "Summon my son!"
translations.idiomatic: He then called Liu Shu and Yuan Yan and said, "Summon my son!"

sentences.zh: 述等將呼太子，上曰：「勇也。」

translations.literal: Shu and the others were about to summon the crown prince; the emperor said: "Yong."
translations.idiomatic: As Shu and the others moved to summon the crown prince, the emperor said, "Yong—not him."

sentences.zh: 述、巖出閣為敕書。

translations.literal: Shu and Yan left the inner chambers to draft an imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: Shu and Yan withdrew to draft an imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 楊素聞之，以白太子，矯詔執述、巖，系大理獄；

translations.literal: Yang Su heard of this, informed the crown prince, and by forged edict arrested Shu and Yan and imprisoned them in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su learned of this, informed the crown prince, and by forged edict had Shu and Yan arrested and thrown into the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 追東宮兵士帖上台宿衛，門禁出入，並取宇文述、郭衍節度；

translations.literal: He recalled Eastern Palace soldiers to post as palace guards on the upper terrace, controlled entry and exit at the gates, and placed all under the command of Yuwen Shu and Guo Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled the Eastern Palace troops to guard the palace, controlled all passage through the gates, and put Yuwen Shu and Guo Yan in overall command.

sentences.zh: 令右庶子張衡入寢殿侍疾，盡遣後宮出就別室；

translations.literal: He ordered Right Vice Mentor Zhang Heng to enter the sleeping hall to attend the illness and sent all the inner palace women out to separate chambers.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Zhang Heng, Right Vice Mentor, into the sickroom and had all the palace women removed to other quarters.

sentences.zh: 俄而上崩。

translations.literal: Shortly the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor was dead.

sentences.zh: 故中外頗有異論。

translations.literal: Therefore inside and outside the court there were rather many differing opinions.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors of foul play soon spread throughout the court and beyond.

sentences.zh: 陳夫人與後宮聞變，相顧戰慄失色。

translations.literal: Lady Chen and the inner palace women, hearing of the change, looked at one another trembling and pale.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chen and the other palace women, hearing what had happened, stared at one another in terror, trembling and pale.

sentences.zh: 晡後，太子遣使者繼小金合，帖紙於際，親署封字，以賜夫人。

translations.literal: After the hour of shen the crown prince sent an envoy bearing a small gilt box, with paper pasted at the seam and the seal characters written in his own hand, to bestow on the lady.
translations.idiomatic: That afternoon the crown prince sent an envoy with a small gilt box, paper pasted over the seam and sealed in his own hand, as a gift for Lady Chen.

sentences.zh: 夫人見之，惶懼，以為鴆毒，不敢發。

translations.literal: When the lady saw it she was fearful and alarmed, thinking it poison, and did not dare open it.
translations.idiomatic: When she saw it she was terrified, thinking it contained poison, and dared not open it.

sentences.zh: 使者促之，乃發，合中有同心結數枚，宮人鹹悅，相謂曰：「得免死矣！」

translations.literal: The envoy urged her; then she opened it. Inside the box were several lover's-knots; the palace women were all pleased and said to one another: "We have escaped death!"
translations.idiomatic: The envoy pressed her, and at last she opened it. Inside were several lover's knots; the palace women rejoiced and said to one another, "We are spared!"

sentences.zh: 陳氏恚而卻坐，不肯致謝；

translations.literal: Lady Chen was resentful and sat back, refusing to offer thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chen, still furious, sat back and refused to thank the envoy.

sentences.zh: 諸宮人共逼之，乃拜使者。

translations.literal: The palace women together pressed her, and only then did she bow to the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The other palace women pressed her until she finally bowed to the envoy.

sentences.zh: 其夜，太子蒸焉。

translations.literal: That night the crown prince had carnal relations with her.
translations.idiomatic: That same night the crown prince took her to his bed.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，發喪，太子即皇帝位。

translations.literal: Day yimao: the mourning procession departed; the crown prince assumed the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: On day yimao the funeral procession set out, and the crown prince ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 會伊州刺史楊約來朝，太子遣約入長安，易留守者，矯稱高祖之詔，賜故太子勇死，縊殺之；

translations.literal: It happened that Yang Yue, governor of Yizhou, came to court; the crown prince sent Yue into Chang'an to replace the garrison commander, and by forged edict in Gaozu's name granted the former crown prince Yong death and had him strangled.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yue, governor of Yizhou, happened to be at court; the crown prince sent him to Chang'an to replace the garrison commander, forged an edict in Gaozu's name ordering the former crown prince Yong to take his own life, and had him strangled.

sentences.zh: 然後陳兵集眾，發高祖凶問。

translations.literal: Only then did he array troops and gather the multitude and announce Gaozu's death.
translations.idiomatic: Only after that did he marshal troops, assemble the officials, and publicly announce Gaozu's death.

sentences.zh: 煬帝聞之，曰：「令兄之弟，果堪大任。」

translations.literal: Emperor Yangdi heard of it and said: "A younger brother of Linggong—truly fit for a great charge."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang heard of it he remarked, "A younger brother in the mold of Linggong—truly equal to a great charge."

sentences.zh: 追封勇為房陵王，不為置嗣。

translations.literal: He posthumously enfeoffed Yong as Prince of Fangling and did not establish an heir for him.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously enfeoffed Yong as Prince of Fangling but appointed no successor to carry on his line.

sentences.zh: 八月，丁卯，梓宮至自仁壽宮；

translations.literal: Eighth month, day dingmao: the coffin arrived from Renshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on day dingmao, the coffin arrived from Renshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 丙子，殯於大興前殿。

translations.literal: Day bingzi: the encoffining at the front hall of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: On day bingzi the body was laid in state in the front hall at Daxing.

sentences.zh: 柳述、元巖並除名，述徙龍川，巖徙南海。

translations.literal: Liu Shu and Yuan Yan were both struck from the registers; Shu was banished to Longchuan, Yan to Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shu and Yuan Yan were both struck from the registers; Shu was exiled to Longchuan and Yan to Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 帝令蘭陵公主與述離絕，欲改嫁之；

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Princess Lanling to sever ties with Shu and intended to marry her to another.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Princess Lanling to divorce Shu and planned to marry her to someone else.

sentences.zh: 公主以死自誓，不復朝謁，上表請與述同徙，帝大怒。

translations.literal: The princess vowed she would rather die, no longer attended court audiences, and submitted a memorial asking to be exiled with Shu; the emperor was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: The princess swore she would rather die, ceased attending court, and submitted a memorial asking to be exiled with Shu; the emperor was furious.

sentences.zh: 公主憂憤而卒，臨終，上表請葬於柳氏。

translations.literal: The princess died of grief and indignation; on her deathbed she submitted a memorial asking to be buried with the Liu clan.
translations.idiomatic: The princess died of grief and anger; on her deathbed she petitioned to be buried in the Liu family plot.

sentences.zh: 帝愈怒，竟不哭，葬送甚薄。

translations.literal: The emperor grew still angrier, would not weep at all, and the funeral was very meager.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew still angrier, refused to weep for her, and gave her a mean funeral.

sentences.zh: 太史令袁充奏言：「皇帝即位，與堯受命年合。」

translations.literal: Director of the Astral Service Yuan Chong memorialized: "The emperor's accession coincides with the year of Yao's receiving the Mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chong, Director of the Astral Service, memorialized that the year of the emperor's accession coincided with the year in which Yao received the Mandate.

sentences.zh: 諷百官表賀。

translations.literal: He hinted that the hundred officials should submit congratulatory memorials.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the officials to submit congratulatory memorials.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎許善心議，以為「國哀甫爾，不宜稱賀。」

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Xu Shansin argued that "the national mourning has only just begun; it is not fitting to offer congratulations."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shansin, Vice Minister of Rites, argued that national mourning had only just begun and congratulations were inappropriate.

sentences.zh: 左衛大將軍宇文述素惡善心，諷御史劾之；

translations.literal: Left Guard General Yuwen Shu had long hated Shansin and hinted that the censor should impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shu, Left Guard General, who had long disliked Xu Shansin, prompted the censors to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 左遷給事郎，降品二等。

translations.literal: "He was demoted to Attendant Gentleman and his rank lowered by two grades."
translations.idiomatic: "Xu Shansin was demoted to Attendant Gentleman and his rank was lowered by two grades."

sentences.zh: 漢王諒有寵於高祖，為并州總管，自山以東，至於滄海，南距黃河，五十二州皆隸焉；

translations.literal: Prince Han Yang Liang had favor with Gaozu and served as governor-general of Bingzhou; from the mountains eastward to the sea, south to the Yellow River, fifty-two prefectures were all subordinate to him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Han, Yang Liang, had been a favorite of Gaozu and held the post of governor-general of Bingzhou; from the eastern mountains to the sea and south to the Yellow River, fifty-two prefectures answered to him.

sentences.zh: 特許以便宜從事，不拘律令。

translations.literal: He was specially permitted to act as expedient required, not bound by statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially authorized to act at his own discretion, unconstrained by the code.

sentences.zh: 諒自以所居天下精兵處，見太子勇以讒廢，居常怏怏，及蜀王秀得罪，尤不自安，陰蓄異圖。

translations.literal: Liang considered that where he dwelt was the place of the empire's finest troops; seeing Crown Prince Yong deposed through slander he was constantly discontented, and when Prince Shu Yang Xiu was punished he was still less at ease, and secretly harbored divergent designs.
translations.idiomatic: Liang knew his territory held the empire's finest troops; after Crown Prince Yong was deposed on false charges he brooded constantly, and when Prince Shu Yang Xiu was punished he grew still more uneasy and began secretly plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 言於高祖，以「突厥方強，宜修武備。」

translations.literal: He told Gaozu that "the Turks are growing strong and military preparations should be strengthened."
translations.idiomatic: He told Gaozu that the Turks were growing strong and that military preparations should be strengthened.

sentences.zh: 於是大發工役，繕治器械，招集亡命，左右私人殆將數萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon he greatly mobilized labor corvée, repaired weapons and equipment, gathered fugitives, and his personal retainers nearly reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu approved, and Liang mobilized vast labor levies, refurbished arms and equipment, recruited fugitives, and gathered nearly ten thousand personal retainers.

sentences.zh: 突厥嘗寇邊，高祖使諒御之，為突厥所敗；

translations.literal: The Turks once raided the frontier; Gaozu had Liang repel them, and he was defeated by the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks once raided the frontier Gaozu sent Liang to repel them, and Liang was defeated.

sentences.zh: 其所領將帥坐除解者八十餘人，皆配防嶺表。

translations.literal: Of the generals and commanders under him who were punished by dismissal, more than eighty were all assigned to garrison duty south of the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: More than eighty of his officers were dismissed and assigned to garrison duty in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 諒以其宿舊，奏請留之，高祖怒曰：「爾為籓王，惟當敬依朝命，何得私論宿舊，廢國家憲法邪！

translations.literal: Liang, on account of their long service, memorialized asking to retain them. Gaozu angrily said: "You are a feudatory prince—you should only respectfully follow court orders. How dare you privately plead for old associates and set aside the state's laws!
translations.idiomatic: Liang petitioned to keep them on account of their long service. Gaozu raged: "You are a feudatory prince—you should obey the court's orders. How dare you plead for old friends and set aside the laws of the state!

sentences.zh: 嗟乎小子，爾一旦無我，或欲妄動，彼取爾如籠內雞雛耳，何用腹心為！」

translations.literal: Alas, boy—once I am gone you may wish to act rashly, but they will take you as easily as chicks in a cage. Of what use are trusted confidants!"
translations.idiomatic: Alas, boy—once I am gone you may be tempted to act rashly, but they will seize you as easily as chicks in a cage. What good will your trusted men do you then!"

sentences.zh: 王頍者，僧辯之子，倜儻好奇略，為諒咨議參軍，蕭摩訶，陳氏舊將，二人俱不得志，每鬱鬱思亂，皆為諒所親善，贊成其陰謀。

translations.literal: Wang Wen was the son of Wang Senbian, bold and unconventional and fond of strange stratagems, and served Liang as advising staff officer. Xiao Mohe was an old general of Chen. Both men were frustrated in their ambitions and constantly brooded on rebellion; both were intimate with Liang and abetted his secret plot.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wen, son of Wang Senbian, was bold, unconventional, and drawn to daring stratagems; he served Liang as advising staff officer. Xiao Mohe was a former Chen general. Both were frustrated men who brooded on rebellion; Liang favored them both, and they encouraged his conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 會熒惑守東井，儀曹鄴人傅奕曉星歷，諒問之曰：「是何祥也？」

translations.literal: It happened that Mars stood guard at the Eastern Well; Fu Yi of Ye, in the Bureau of Ceremonies, understood astronomy and calendrics. Liang asked him: "What omen is this?"
translations.idiomatic: When Mars came to station at the Eastern Well, Liang questioned Fu Yi of Ye, an official in the Bureau of Ceremonies skilled in astronomy, and asked, "What omen does this portend?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「天上東井，黃道所經，熒惑過之，乃其常理，若入地上井，則可怪耳。」

translations.literal: He replied: "The Eastern Well in the heavens lies on the ecliptic; for Mars to pass it is its regular course—only if it entered an earthly well would it be strange."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yi replied, "The Eastern Well in the heavens lies on the ecliptic; for Mars to pass through it is perfectly ordinary—it would be strange only if it fell into a well on earth."

sentences.zh: 諒不悅。

translations.literal: Liang was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was displeased.

sentences.zh: 及高祖崩，煬帝遣車騎將軍屈突通以高祖璽書征之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu died, Emperor Yangdi dispatched Cavalry General Qutu Tong with Gaozu's imperial-seal summons to recall him.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu's death Emperor Yang sent Cavalry General Qutu Tong with an imperial summons bearing Gaozu's seal to recall him to court.

sentences.zh: 先是，高祖與諒密約：「若璽書召汝，敕字傍別加一點，又與玉麟符合者，當就征。」

translations.literal: Earlier Gaozu and Liang had a secret agreement: "If an imperial-seal summons recalls you, with an extra dot beside the character for 'edict' and matching the jade tally, then you should obey the summons."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu and Liang had earlier agreed in secret: "If a summons with the imperial seal recalls you, look for an extra dot beside the character for 'edict' and a matching jade tally—only then obey the call."

sentences.zh: 及發書無驗，諒知有變。

translations.literal: When the document was issued and the signs were absent, Liang knew there was a change.
translations.idiomatic: When the document arrived without those signs, Liang knew something was wrong.

sentences.zh: 詰通，通占對不屈，乃遣歸長安。

translations.literal: He interrogated Tong; Tong answered firmly without yielding, and Liang then sent him back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He questioned Qutu Tong, who answered firmly and would not yield; Liang then sent him back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 諒遂發兵反。

translations.literal: Liang thereupon raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Liang thereupon rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 總管司馬安定皇甫誕切諫，諒不納。

translations.literal: Governor-general's aide Huangfu Yan of Anding remonstrated urgently; Liang did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Yan of Anding, the governor-general's chief aide, remonstrated urgently, but Liang would not listen.

sentences.zh: 誕流涕曰：「竊料大王兵資非京師之敵；

translations.literal: Yan said with tears: "I venture to estimate that the prince's military resources are no match for the capital's forces.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Yan said through his tears, "I venture to judge that Your Highness's forces cannot match those of the capital.

sentences.zh: 加以君臣位定，逆順勢殊，士馬雖精，難以取勝。

translations.literal: Moreover, ruler and minister have fixed positions; the rebellious and the loyal differ in momentum; though troops and horses be elite, victory will be hard to win.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the throne is settled, the moral advantage lies with the loyal side, and however fine your troops and horses, victory will be hard to win.

sentences.zh: 一旦陷身叛逆，絓於刑書，雖欲為布衣，不可得也。」

translations.literal: Once you fall into rebellion and are caught in the penal code, even if you wished to be a commoner it could not be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: Once you are branded a rebel and caught in the law, not even the life of a commoner will be yours."

sentences.zh: 諒怒，囚之。

translations.literal: Liang was angry and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang flew into a rage and had him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 嵐州刺史喬鐘葵將赴諒，其司馬京兆陶模拒之曰：「漢王所圖不軌，公荷國厚恩，當竭誠效命，豈得身為厲階乎！」

translations.literal: Qiao Zhongkui, governor of Lanzhou, was about to go to join Liang; his aide Tao Mo of Jingzhao refused and said: "Prince Han's designs are improper; you bear the state's deep grace and should exhaust loyalty in service—how can you make yourself a stepping-stone to disaster!"
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhongkui, governor of Lanzhou, was preparing to join Liang when his chief aide Tao Mo of Jingzhao refused, saying, "Prince Han's plot is treasonous. You owe the state a great debt of gratitude and should serve it with all your heart—how can you make yourself the instrument of his ruin!"

sentences.zh: 鐘葵失色曰：「司馬反邪！」

translations.literal: Zhongkui blanched and said: "Aide, are you rebelling?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkui turned pale and cried, "Aide—are you rebelling against me?"

sentences.zh: 臨之以兵，辭氣不撓，鐘葵義而釋之。

translations.literal: He confronted him with troops, but Mo's tone did not bend; Zhongkui, admiring his integrity, released him.
translations.idiomatic: He threatened him with armed men, but Tao Mo's tone did not waver; impressed by his integrity, Zhongkui let him go.

sentences.zh: 軍吏曰：「若不斬模，無以壓眾心。」

translations.literal: A military officer said: "If Mo is not beheaded, there is no way to suppress the troops' minds."
translations.idiomatic: An officer said, "Unless you execute Mo, you cannot keep the men in line."

sentences.zh: 乃囚之。

translations.literal: He was then imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkui had him imprisoned instead.

sentences.zh: 於是從諒反者凡十九州。

translations.literal: Thereupon those who followed Liang in rebellion numbered nineteen prefectures in all.
translations.idiomatic: In all, nineteen prefectures joined Liang's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 王頍說諒曰：「王所部將吏，家屬盡在關西，若用此等，則宜長驅深入，直據京都，所謂疾雷不及掩耳；

translations.literal: Wang Wen advised Liang: "The officers and officials under the prince—all their families are in Guanxi. If you use such men, you should drive deep in a long march and seize the capital directly—the so-called swift thunder that does not allow one to cover the ears.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wen urged Liang, "Your officers' families are all in Guanxi. If you rely on such men you must drive deep and strike straight for the capital—the thunderclap that gives no time to cover one's ears.

sentences.zh: 若但欲割據舊齊之地，宜任東人。」

translations.literal: If you only wish to carve out and hold the old Qi territory, you should employ easterners."
translations.idiomatic: If you only mean to hold the old Qi lands, you should rely on men from the east.

sentences.zh: 諒不能決，乃兼用二策，唱言楊素反，將誅之。

translations.literal: Liang could not decide and therefore used both strategies together, proclaiming that Yang Su had rebelled and that he would execute him."
translations.idiomatic: Liang could not choose between them and tried both at once, declaring that Yang Su had rebelled and that he would put him to death."

sentences.zh: 總管府兵曹聞喜裴文安說諒曰：「井陘以西，在王掌握之內，山東士馬，亦為我有，宜悉發之；

translations.literal: Pei Wen'an of Wenxi, military registrar of the governor-general's office, advised Liang: "West of Jingxing is within the prince's grasp, and Shandong's troops and horses are also ours—you should mobilize them all.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Wen'an of Wenxi, military registrar on Liang's staff, urged him, "Everything west of Jingxing is in your hands, and the armies of Shandong are yours as well—you should mobilize them all.

sentences.zh: 分遣羸兵屯守要害，仍命隨方略地，帥其精銳，直入蒲津。

translations.literal: Send weak troops in detachments to garrison key points, then order them to advance as circumstances allow and lead the elite straight into Pujin.
translations.idiomatic: Post weak detachments at the key passes, then lead your best troops straight for Pujin.

sentences.zh: 文安請為前鋒，王以大軍繼後，風行雷擊，頓於霸上。

translations.literal: Wen'an asked to serve as vanguard while the prince followed with the main army—swift as wind, sudden as thunder—and encamped at Bashang.
translations.idiomatic: Let me take the vanguard while Your Highness follows with the main army—we will strike like wind and thunder and halt at Bashang.

sentences.zh: 咸陽以東，可指麾而定。

translations.literal: East of Xianyang can be settled at a wave of the hand.
translations.idiomatic: Everything east of Xianyang will fall at a gesture.

sentences.zh: 京師震擾，兵不暇集，上下相疑，群情離駭；

translations.literal: The capital will be shaken and disturbed, troops will have no time to assemble, above and below will suspect one another, and the multitude will scatter in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The capital will panic, troops will not have time to gather, court and camp will turn on one another, and the people will scatter in terror.

sentences.zh: 我陳兵號令，誰敢不從！

translations.literal: When we array troops and issue commands, who will dare not obey!
translations.idiomatic: Once we parade our forces and issue our orders, who will dare disobey!

sentences.zh: 旬日之間，事可定矣。」

translations.literal: Within ten days the affair can be settled."
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days the matter will be settled."

sentences.zh: 諒大悅，於是遣所署大將軍余公理出太谷，趣河陽，大將軍綦良出滏口，趣黎陽，大將軍劉建出井陘，略燕、趙，柱國喬鐘葵出雁門，署文安為柱國，與柱國紇單貴、王聃等直指京師。

translations.literal: Liang was greatly pleased and thereupon dispatched his appointed Grand General Yu Gongli out through Taigu toward Heyang, Grand General Qi Liang out through Fukou toward Liyang, Grand General Liu Jian out through Jingxing to overrun Yan and Zhao, and Pillar Duke Qiao Zhongkui out through Yanmen; he appointed Wen'an Pillar Duke, and with Pillar Dukes Heda Gui, Wang Dan, and others drove straight for the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was delighted and sent his appointed generals in every direction: Yu Gongli through Taigu toward Heyang, Qi Liang through Fukou toward Liyang, Liu Jian through Jingxing to overrun Yan and Zhao, and Qiao Zhongkui through Yanmen. He made Wen'an a Pillar Duke and, with Heda Gui, Wang Dan, and others, marched straight on the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝以右武衛將軍洛陽丘和為蒲州刺史，鎮蒲津。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Qiu He of Luoyang, Right Martial Guard General, governor of Puzhou to guard Pujin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Qiu He of Luoyang, Right Martial Guard General, governor of Puzhou to hold Pujin.

sentences.zh: 諒簡精銳數百騎戴羃，詐稱諒宮人還長安，門司弗覺，逕入蒲州，城中豪傑亦有應之者；

translations.literal: Liang selected several hundred elite horsemen wearing veils, falsely claiming to be palace women of Liang returning to Chang'an; the gate guards did not notice and they entered Puzhou directly; eminent men in the city also responded to them.
translations.idiomatic: Liang picked several hundred elite horsemen in disguise, pretending to be his palace women returning to Chang'an. The gate guards never noticed, and they rode straight into Puzhou, where local leaders rallied to them.

sentences.zh: 丘和覺其變，逾城，逃歸長安。

translations.literal: Qiu He perceived the change, climbed over the wall, and fled back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu He sensed the plot, climbed over the wall, and fled to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 蒲州長史勃海高義明、司馬北平榮毘皆為反者所執。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Gao Yiming of Bohai and Vice Administrator Rong Pi of Beiping in Puzhou were both seized by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yiming of Bohai, chief administrator of Puzhou, and Rong Pi of Beiping, vice administrator, were both taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 裴文安等未至蒲津百餘里，諒忽改圖，令紇單貴斷河橋，守蒲州，而召文安還。

translations.literal: When Pei Wen'an and the others were still more than a hundred li from Pujin, Liang suddenly changed his plan, ordered Heda Gui to cut the river bridge and hold Puzhou, and recalled Wen'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Wen'an was still more than a hundred li from Pujin, Liang suddenly changed his mind, ordered Heda Gui to destroy the river bridge and hold Puzhou, and recalled Wen'an.

sentences.zh: 文安至，謂諒曰：「兵機詭速，本欲出其不意。

translations.literal: When Wen'an arrived he said to Liang: "Military opportunity is treacherous and swift; the aim was to strike where they did not expect.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen'an arrived he told Liang, "War depends on speed and surprise—that was the whole point of this plan.

sentences.zh: 王既不行，文安又返，使彼計成，大事去矣。」

translations.literal: The prince did not go, and Wen'an has returned—this lets their plans succeed; the great affair is lost."
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness would not advance, and now I am recalled as well—the enemy will have time to prepare, and the cause is lost."

sentences.zh: 諒不對。

translations.literal: Liang did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Liang made no answer.

sentences.zh: 以王聃為蒲州刺史，裴文安為晉州刺史，薛粹為絳州刺史，梁菩薩為潞州刺史，韋道正為韓州刺史，張伯英為澤州刺史。

translations.literal: He appointed Wang Dan governor of Puzhou, Pei Wen'an governor of Jinzhou, Xue Cui governor of Jiangzhou, Liang Pusa governor of Luzhou, Wei Daozheng governor of Hanzhou, and Zhang Boying governor of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Wang Dan governor of Puzhou, Pei Wen'an of Jinzhou, Xue Cui of Jiangzhou, Liang Pusa of Luzhou, Wei Daozheng of Hanzhou, and Zhang Boying of Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 代州總管天水李景發兵拒諒，諒遣其將劉暠襲景；

translations.literal: Li Jing of Tianshui, governor-general of Daizhou, raised troops to resist Liang; Liang sent his general Liu Gao to attack Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing of Tianshui, governor-general of Daizhou, raised troops to resist Liang, who sent his general Liu Gao against him.

sentences.zh: 景擊斬之。

translations.literal: Jing attacked and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Jing attacked and killed him.

sentences.zh: 諒復遣喬鐘葵帥勁勇三萬攻之，景戰士不過數千，加以城池不固，為鐘葵所攻，崩毀相繼，景且戰且築，士卒皆殊死鬥；

translations.literal: Liang again sent Qiao Zhongkui leading thirty thousand crack troops to attack him. Jing's fighting men numbered only a few thousand; moreover the walls were not solid—under Zhongkui's assault they collapsed one after another. Jing fought while building, and his soldiers all fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent Qiao Zhongkui with thirty thousand crack troops against him. Jing had only a few thousand men, and his walls were weak; under assault they crumbled section by section. Jing fought while rebuilding, and his men battled to the death.

sentences.zh: 鐘葵屢敗。

translations.literal: Zhongkui was repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkui was beaten again and again.

sentences.zh: 司馬馮孝慈、司法呂玉並驍勇善戰，儀同三司侯莫陳乂多謀畫，工拒守之術，景知三人可用，推誠任之，己無所關預，唯在閤持重，時撫循而已。

translations.literal: Vice Administrator Feng Xiaoci and judicial officer Lü Yu were both valiant and skilled in battle; Senior General of the Third Rank Hou Mo Chen Yi was full of stratagems and adept at defensive tactics. Jing knew the three could be used, entrusted them sincerely, and himself intervened in nothing—only sat in the hall with grave bearing and from time to time comforted the troops.
translations.idiomatic: His vice administrator Feng Xiaoci and judicial officer Lü Yu were both fierce fighters; Senior General Hou Mo Chen Yi was a master of strategy and defense. Jing entrusted them fully and intervened in nothing himself—he merely sat in council, steady and grave, and encouraged the men from time to time.

sentences.zh: 楊素將輕騎五千襲王聃、紇單貴於蒲州，夜，至河際，收商賈船，得數百艘，船內多置草，踐之無聲，遂銜枚而濟；

translations.literal: Yang Su led five thousand light cavalry to strike Wang Dan and Heda Gui at Puzhou. At night he reached the riverbank, collected merchant boats, and obtained several hundred vessels; he placed much straw inside the boats so that treading on them made no sound, and thus crossed with reeds in the soldiers' mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su led five thousand light cavalry against Wang Dan and Heda Gui at Puzhou. By night he reached the river, commandeered hundreds of merchant boats, lined them with straw so footsteps made no sound, and crossed with reeds clenched in the men's teeth.

sentences.zh: 遲明，擊之；

translations.literal: At dawn he attacked them.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he attacked.

sentences.zh: 紇單貴敗走，聃懼，以城降。

translations.literal: Heda Gui was defeated and fled; Dan was afraid and surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Heda Gui was routed and fled; Dan, terrified, surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 有詔征素還。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Su recalled.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled Su to court.

sentences.zh: 初，素將行，計日破賊，皆如所量，於是以素為并州道行軍總管、河北道安撫大使，帥眾數萬以討諒。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Su was about to depart, he calculated the days to defeat the rebels—and all matched his estimates. Thereupon he was made campaign commander of the Bingzhou circuit and pacification commissioner of the Hebei circuit, leading tens of thousands to suppress Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Su had first set out he had predicted the day of victory—and been right. The emperor now made him campaign commander on the Bingzhou front and pacification commissioner for Hebei, with tens of thousands of men to crush Liang.

sentences.zh: 諒之初起兵也，妃兄豆盧毓為府主簿，苦諫，不從，私謂其弟懿曰：「吾匹馬歸朝，自得免禍，此乃身計，非為國也。

translations.literal: When Liang first raised troops, his consort's elder brother Doulu Yu served as chief clerk of the princely establishment. He remonstrated urgently but was not obeyed, and privately told his younger brother Yi: "If I return to court alone on horseback I can escape disaster myself—this is a plan for my person, not for the state.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang first rebelled, his consort's brother Doulu Yu was chief clerk on his staff. Yu remonstrated in vain, then told his brother Yi in private, "If I ride alone back to court I can save myself—that is a plan for my own skin, not for the realm.

sentences.zh: 不若且偽從之，徐伺其使。」

translations.literal: Better to feign compliance for now and slowly watch for an opportunity."
translations.idiomatic: Better to pretend to go along and watch for my chance."

sentences.zh: 毓，勣之子也。

translations.literal: Yu was the son of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was a son of Li Ji.

sentences.zh: 毓兄顯州刺史賢言於帝曰：「臣弟毓素懷志節，必不從亂，但逼凶威，不能自遂。

translations.literal: Yu's elder brother Xian, governor of Xianzhou, said to the emperor: "My younger brother Yu has long cherished integrity and will surely not follow the rebellion, but he is compelled by brutal power and cannot carry out his will.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's elder brother Xian, governor of Xianzhou, told the emperor, "My brother Yu has always been a man of principle and will not join the rebellion, but Liang's power holds him in check.

sentences.zh: 臣請從軍，與毓為表裡，諒不足圖也。」

translations.literal: I ask to join the army and act inside and outside with Yu—Liang cannot be plotted against."
translations.idiomatic: Let me join the campaign and work with him from within and without—Liang will be easy to bring down."

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 賢密遣家人繼敕書至毓所，與之計議。

translations.literal: Xian secretly sent a family member following upon the imperial edict to Yu's place to plan with him.
translations.idiomatic: Xian secretly sent a servant after the imperial edict to confer with Yu.

sentences.zh: 諒出城，將往介州，令毓與總管屬朱濤留守。

translations.literal: Liang left the city, intending to go to Jiezhou, and ordered Yu and the governor-general's aide Zhu Tao to remain on guard.
translations.idiomatic: Liang left the city for Jiezhou and left Yu and Zhu Tao, an aide on his staff, to hold the capital.

sentences.zh: 毓謂濤曰：「漢王構逆，敗不旋踵，吾屬豈可坐受夷滅，孤負國家邪！

translations.literal: Yu said to Tao: "Prince Han has raised rebellion; defeat will come in no time. How can we sit and await extermination, failing the state!
translations.idiomatic: Yu told Tao, "Prince Han's rebellion will collapse any day now. Shall we sit here and wait to be wiped out and betray the state!

sentences.zh: 當與卿出兵拒之。」

translations.literal: I should join with you in raising troops to resist him."
translations.idiomatic: I must join with you and raise troops to resist him."

sentences.zh: 濤驚曰：「王以大事相付，何得有是語！」

translations.literal: Tao was alarmed and said: "The prince entrusted us with a great charge—how can there be such talk!"
translations.idiomatic: Tao cried in alarm, "The prince entrusted us with a great charge—how can you speak so!

sentences.zh: 因拂衣而去，毓追斬之。

translations.literal: He thereupon swept his robes and left; Yu pursued and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He turned to leave; Yu ran him down and killed him.

sentences.zh: 出皇甫誕於獄，與之協計，及開府儀同三司宿勤武等閉城拒諒。

translations.literal: He released Huangfu Yan from prison, plotted with him, and together with Senior General Suqin Wu and others closed the city to resist Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He freed Huangfu Yan from prison, plotted with him, and with Senior General Suqin Wu and others shut the gates against Liang.

sentences.zh: 部分未定，有人告諒，諒襲擊之。

translations.literal: The dispositions were not yet settled when someone informed Liang, and Liang launched a surprise attack.
translations.idiomatic: Before the dispositions were complete someone informed Liang, and he struck at once.

sentences.zh: 毓見諒至，紿其眾曰：「此賊軍也！」

translations.literal: When Yu saw Liang arrive he deceived the troops, saying: "These are bandit forces!"
translations.idiomatic: When Yu saw Liang approach he cried to the troops, "These are enemy soldiers!"

sentences.zh: 諒攻城南門，稽胡守南城，不識諒，射之；

translations.literal: Liang attacked the south gate; Jiehu tribesmen guarded the south wall, did not recognize Liang, and shot at him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang attacked the south gate. Jiehu guards on the wall did not recognize him and shot at him.

sentences.zh: 矢下如雨；

translations.literal: Arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Arrows fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 諒移攻西門，守兵識諒，即開門納之，毓、誕皆死。

translations.literal: Liang shifted to attack the west gate; the guards recognized Liang and at once opened the gate to admit him. Yu and Yan both died.
translations.idiomatic: Liang turned to the west gate; the guards there recognized him and opened the gates. Yu and Yan were both killed.

sentences.zh: 綦良攻慈州刺史上官政，不克，引兵攻行相州事薛冑，又不克，遂自滏口攻黎州，塞白馬津。

translations.literal: Qi Liang attacked Shangguan Zheng, governor of Cizhou, but could not take him; he led troops to attack Xue Zhou, acting administrator of Xiangzhou, and again failed; he then advanced from Fukou to attack Lizhou and blocked Baima Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Liang attacked the governor of Cizhou, Shangguan Zheng, without success, then turned on Xue Zhou, acting administrator of Xiangzhou, and failed again. He advanced from Fukou against Lizhou and blocked Baima Ford.

sentences.zh: 余公理自太行下河內，帝以右衛將軍史祥為行軍總管，軍於河陰。

translations.literal: Yu Gongli came down from the Taihang range into Henei; the emperor appointed Shi Xiang, Right Guard General, campaign commander, encamped at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Gongli came down from the Taihang into Henei; the emperor sent Shi Xiang, Right Guard General, as campaign commander to encamp at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 祥謂軍吏曰：「余公理輕而無謀，恃眾而驕，不足破也。」

translations.literal: Xiang said to his officers: "Yu Gongli is frivolous and without stratagem, relying on numbers and arrogant—he is not worth breaking."
translations.idiomatic: Xiang told his officers, "Yu Gongli is rash and stupid, swollen with his numbers—he is nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 公理屯河陽，祥具舟南岸，公理聚兵當之。

translations.literal: Gongli encamped at Heyang; Xiang prepared boats on the south bank, and Gongli massed troops to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Gongli encamped at Heyang; Xiang lined boats on the south bank, and Gongli massed his men to meet him.

sentences.zh: 祥簡精銳於下流潛濟，公理聞之，引兵拒之，戰於須水。

translations.literal: Xiang selected elite troops to cross secretly downstream; when Gongli heard of it he led troops to resist, and they fought at the Xu River.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang picked elite troops to ford downstream in secret. Gongli heard and marched to meet him; they fought at the Xu River.

sentences.zh: 公理未成列，祥擊之，公理大敗。

translations.literal: Before Gongli could form ranks Xiang struck him, and Gongli was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Before Gongli could form his line Xiang struck, and Gongli was routed.

sentences.zh: 祥東趣黎陽，綦良軍不戰而潰。

translations.literal: Xiang pressed east toward Liyang; Qi Liang's army collapsed without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang pressed east to Liyang; Qi Liang's army fled without a fight.

sentences.zh: 祥，寧之子也。

translations.literal: Xiang was the son of Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was a son of Shi Ning.

sentences.zh: 帝將發幽州兵，疑幽州總管竇抗有貳心，問可使取抗者於楊素，素薦前江州刺史勃海李子雄，授上大將軍，拜廣州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to mobilize Youzhou troops and suspected Dou Kang, governor-general of Youzhou, of divided loyalty. He asked Yang Su who could seize Kang; Su recommended Li Zixiong of Bohai, former governor of Jiangzhou, appointed him Grand General, and enfeoffed him as governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned to mobilize Youzhou troops but suspected Dou Kang, governor-general of Youzhou, of disloyalty. He asked Yang Su whom to send; Su recommended Li Zixiong of Bohai, former governor of Jiangzhou, made him a Grand General, and sent him as governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 又以左領軍將軍長孫晟為相州刺史，發山東兵，與李子雄共經略之。

translations.literal: He also appointed Zhangsun Sheng, Left Army General, governor of Xiangzhou, mobilized Shandong troops, and together with Li Zixiong directed operations.
translations.idiomatic: He also appointed Zhangsun Sheng, Left Army General, governor of Xiangzhou, raised Shandong troops, and joined Li Zixiong in the campaign.

sentences.zh: 晟辭以男行布在諒所部，帝曰：「公體國之深，終不以兒害義，朕今相委，公其勿辭。」

translations.literal: Sheng declined on the ground that his son Xingbu was in Liang's domain. The emperor said: "Sir, your devotion to the state runs deep; in the end you will not let a son harm righteousness. I now entrust this to you—do not decline."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng declined, saying his son Xingbu was in Liang's territory. The emperor said, "Your loyalty to the state runs too deep for a son to sway you. I entrust this to you—do not refuse."

sentences.zh: 李子雄馳至幽州，止傳捨，召募得千餘人。

translations.literal: Li Zixiong galloped to Youzhou, stopped at a relay station, and recruited more than a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zixiong raced to Youzhou, lodged at a relay station, and raised more than a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 抗來詣子雄，子雄伏甲擒之。

translations.literal: Kang came to visit Zixiong; Zixiong had armed men in hiding seize him.
translations.idiomatic: When Kang came to call on him, Zixiong's hidden guards seized him.

sentences.zh: 抗，榮定之子也。

translations.literal: Kang was the son of Rongding.
translations.idiomatic: Kang was a son of Dou Rongding.

sentences.zh: 子雄遂發幽州兵步騎三萬，自井陘西擊諒。

translations.literal: Zixiong thereupon mobilized thirty thousand infantry and cavalry from Youzhou and attacked Liang from the west through Jingxing.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiong then led thirty thousand Youzhou infantry and cavalry west through Jingxing against Liang.

sentences.zh: 時劉建圍戍將京兆張祥於井陘，子雄破建於抱犢山下，建遁去。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Jian was besieging the garrison commander Zhang Xiang of Jingzhao at Jingxing; Zixiong defeated Jian at the foot of Mount Baodu and Jian fled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian was then besieging the garrison commander Zhang Xiang of Jingzhao at Jingxing; Zixiong defeated him at Mount Baodu and Jian fled.

sentences.zh: 李景被圍月餘，詔朔州刺史代人楊義臣救之。

translations.literal: Li Jing had been besieged for more than a month; an edict ordered Yang Yichen of Dairen, governor of Shuozhou, to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing had been besieged for more than a month when the emperor ordered Yang Yichen of Dairen, governor of Shuozhou, to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 義臣帥馬步二萬，夜出西陘，喬鐘葵悉眾拒之。

translations.literal: Yichen led twenty thousand horse and foot, marched out by night through the western pass, and Qiao Zhongkui opposed him with his entire force.
translations.idiomatic: Yichen led twenty thousand horse and foot out by night through the western pass; Qiao Zhongkui met him with his full army.

sentences.zh: 義臣自以兵少，悉取軍中牛驢，得數千頭，復令兵數百人，人持一鼓潛驅之，匿於澗谷間。

translations.literal: Yichen considered his troops few, took all the oxen and donkeys in the army—several thousand head—and again ordered several hundred soldiers, each holding a drum, to drive them secretly and hide them in ravines and valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking his force too small, Yichen collected several thousand oxen and donkeys from the army and hid several hundred men with drums among the ravines to drive them.

sentences.zh: 晡後，義臣復與鐘葵戰，兵初合，命驅牛驢者疾進，一時鳴鼓，塵埃張天，鐘葵軍不知，以為伏兵發，因而奔潰；

translations.literal: After the hour of shen Yichen again fought Zhongkui; as the troops first joined he ordered those driving the oxen and donkeys to advance swiftly, and at once the drums sounded, dust filled the sky, and Zhongkui's army, not knowing, thought ambush troops had risen and therefore fled in collapse.
translations.idiomatic: In the afternoon Yichen engaged Zhongkui again. As the lines met he signaled the drovers forward; drums burst out at once, dust filled the sky, and Zhongkui's men, thinking an ambush had sprung, broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 義臣縱擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Yichen pursued and utterly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yichen pursued and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 晉、絳、呂三州皆為諒城守，楊素各以二千人縻之而去。

translations.literal: The three prefectures of Jin, Jiang, and Lü all held their cities for Liang; Yang Su left two thousand men each to pin them down and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectures of Jin, Jiang, and Lü all held their cities for Liang; Yang Su left two thousand men at each to pin them down and marched on.

sentences.zh: 諒遣其將趙子開擁眾十餘萬，柵絕徑路，屯據高壁，布陳五十里。

translations.literal: Liang sent his general Zhao Zikai leading a host of more than a hundred thousand, palisading the paths, holding high ramparts, and arraying battle lines for fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent his general Zhao Zikai with more than a hundred thousand men, blocking the passes, holding the heights, and drawing up a line fifty li long.

sentences.zh: 素令諸將以兵臨之，自引奇兵潛入霍山，緣崖谷而進。

translations.literal: Su ordered the generals to press them with troops while he himself led picked troops secretly into Mount Huo, advancing along cliffs and valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Su ordered his generals to pin the enemy in front while he led picked troops secretly through Mount Huo along the cliffs and ravines.

sentences.zh: 素營於谷口，自坐營外，使軍司入營簡留三百人守營，軍士憚北兵之強，不欲出戰，多願守營，因爾致遲。

translations.literal: Su encamped at the mouth of the valley, himself sitting outside the camp, and had the army registrar enter the camp to select three hundred men to guard it. The soldiers feared the strength of the northern troops and did not wish to fight; many wished to remain in camp, and thus delay occurred.
translations.idiomatic: Su camped at the mouth of the valley and sat outside the lines while his registrar chose three hundred men to hold the camp. The soldiers feared the northern army's strength and hung back, many preferring to stay in camp, which caused delay.

sentences.zh: 素責所由，軍司具對，素即召所留三百人出營，悉斬之；

translations.literal: Su blamed those responsible; the army registrar answered in full, and Su at once summoned the three hundred left in camp outside and beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: Su demanded an explanation; when the registrar answered, Su had the three hundred men brought out and beheaded every one of them.

sentences.zh: 更令簡留，人皆無願留者。

translations.literal: He again ordered a selection to remain; no one wished to stay.
translations.idiomatic: He called for volunteers to stay behind; not a man stepped forward.

sentences.zh: 素乃引軍馳進，出北軍之北，直指其營，鳴鼓縱火；

translations.literal: Su then led the army in a swift advance, emerging north of the northern army's north flank, drove straight at their camp, beat drums, and set fires.
translations.idiomatic: Su then charged forward, swung around behind the northern army, struck straight at their camp, beat the drums, and set fires.

sentences.zh: 北軍不知所為，自相蹂踐，殺傷數萬。

translations.literal: The northern army did not know what to do, trampled one another, and tens of thousands were killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: The northern army panicked, trampled one another, and tens of thousands were killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 諒所署介州刺史梁修羅屯介休，聞素至，棄城走。

translations.literal: Liang Xiuluo, whom Liang had appointed governor of Jiezhou, was encamped at Jiexiu; hearing that Su had arrived, he abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Xiuluo, Liang's appointee as governor of Jiezhou, was at Jiexiu; when he heard Su was coming he abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 諒聞趙子開敗，大懼，自將眾且十萬，拒素於蒿澤。

translations.literal: When Liang heard that Zhao Zikai was defeated he was greatly afraid, personally led a host of nearly a hundred thousand, and opposed Su at Haose Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang heard of Zhao Zikai's defeat he was terrified and personally led nearly a hundred thousand men to face Su at Haose Marsh.

sentences.zh: 會大雨，諒欲引軍還，王頍諫曰：「楊素懸軍深入，士馬疲弊，王以銳卒自將擊之，其勢必克。

translations.literal: It happened to rain heavily; Liang wished to withdraw the army. Wang Wen remonstrated: "Yang Su's army is deep in hostile territory and his men and horses are worn out. If the prince leads crack troops in person to strike him, victory is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rain fell, and Liang wanted to withdraw. Wang Wen urged him, "Yang Su is deep in enemy country with exhausted men and horses. If Your Highness leads your best troops against him in person, you are sure to win.

sentences.zh: 今望敵而退，示人以怯，沮戰士之心，益西軍之氣，願王勿還。」

translations.literal: Now to withdraw on sight of the enemy shows others your timidity, dampens the warriors' hearts, and increases the western army's morale. I hope the prince will not return."
translations.idiomatic: To retreat at the sight of the enemy shows cowardice, breaks your men's spirit, and heartens the western army. I beg Your Highness not to turn back."

sentences.zh: 諒不從，退守清源。

translations.literal: Liang did not obey and withdrew to defend Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liang would not listen and fell back to Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 王頍謂其子曰：「氣候殊不佳，兵必敗，汝可隨我。」

translations.literal: Wang Wen said to his son: "The signs are very poor; the army will surely be defeated. You may follow me."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wen told his son, "The omens are terrible—the army will lose. Come with me."

sentences.zh: 楊素進擊諒，大破之，擒蕭摩訶。

translations.literal: Yang Su advanced and attacked Liang, utterly defeated him, and captured Xiao Mohe.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su attacked and routed Liang, capturing Xiao Mohe.

sentences.zh: 諒退保晉陽，素進兵圍之，諒窮蹙，請降，餘黨悉平。

translations.literal: Liang withdrew to hold Jinyang; Su advanced and besieged him. Liang, cornered, asked to surrender, and the remaining partisans were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Liang retreated to Jinyang; Su besieged him until, desperate, he surrendered and the last of his followers were crushed.

sentences.zh: 帝遣楊約繼手詔勞素。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Yang Yue with successive handwritten edicts to console Su.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Yang Yue with repeated personal edicts to congratulate Su.

sentences.zh: 王頍將奔突厥，至山中，逕路斷絕，知必不免，謂其子曰：「吾之計數不減楊素，但坐言不見從，遂至於此，不能坐受擒獲，以成豎子名。

translations.literal: Wang Wen was about to flee to the Turks; reaching the mountains he found the paths cut off, knew he could not escape, and said to his son: "My stratagems are no less than Yang Su's, but because my words were not followed I have come to this. I cannot sit and be captured to make a name for some stripling.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wen tried to flee to the Turks; in the mountains the paths were blocked, and knowing he could not escape he told his son, "My plans were no worse than Yang Su's, but no one listened, and so it has come to this. I will not sit here to be captured and make some boy's reputation.

sentences.zh: 吾死之後，汝慎勿過親故。」

translations.literal: After my death you must be careful not to visit kin and old friends."
translations.idiomatic: After I am dead, do not go near kin or old friends."

sentences.zh: 於是自殺，瘞之石窟中。

translations.literal: Thereupon he killed himself and was buried in a stone cave.
translations.idiomatic: He killed himself and was buried in a stone cave.

sentences.zh: 其子數日不得食，遂過其故人，竟為所擒；

translations.literal: His son went several days without food, then visited an old friend and in the end was seized by him.
translations.idiomatic: His son went hungry for days, then visited an old friend and was captured.

sentences.zh: 並獲頍屍，梟於晉陽。

translations.literal: Wen's corpse was also obtained and exposed at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wen's corpse was dug up and displayed at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 群臣奏漢王諒當死，帝不許，除名為民，絕其屬籍，竟以幽死。

translations.literal: The ministers memorialized that Prince Han Yang Liang deserved death; the emperor did not permit it, struck his name from the registers, cut off his clan registry, and in the end he died in confinement.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers urged that Prince Han Yang Liang be put to death; the emperor refused, struck his name from the registers, cut him off from the imperial clan, and in the end he died in confinement.

sentences.zh: 諒所部吏民坐諒死徙者二十餘萬家。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners in Liang's domain who were punished by death or exile on account of Liang numbered more than two hundred thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: More than two hundred thousand households among Liang's officials and people were executed or exiled for his rebellion.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖與獨孤後甚相愛重，誓無異生之子，嘗謂群臣曰：「前世天子，溺於嬖倖，嫡庶分爭，遂有廢立，或至亡國；

translations.literal: Earlier Gaozu and Empress Dugu loved and esteemed each other deeply, swore there would be no sons by other mothers, and once told the ministers: "Emperors of former ages, drowning in favorites, let legitimate and secondary sons contend, and thus there were depositions and enthronements, sometimes even loss of the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning Gaozu and Empress Dugu loved each other deeply and swore they would have no sons by other women. Gaozu once told his ministers, "Emperors of old drowned in favorites, let legitimate and illegitimate sons fight, deposed and enthroned at will, and sometimes lost their kingdoms altogether.

sentences.zh: 朕旁無姬侍，五子同母，可謂真兄弟也，豈有此憂邪！」

translations.literal: I have no concubines at my side; my five sons share one mother—they may be called true brothers. How could there be such worry!"
translations.idiomatic: I have no concubines at my side; my five sons share one mother—they are true brothers. What need is there for such worry!"

sentences.zh: 帝又懲周室諸王微弱，故使諸子分據大鎮，專制方面，權侔帝室。

translations.literal: The emperor also took warning from the Zhou house's princes being weak, and therefore had his sons each hold great territories, monopolizing their regions with power equal to the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also took warning from the weakness of the Zhou princes and gave each son a great territory to rule in his own right, with power rivaling the throne.

sentences.zh: 及其晚節，父子兄弟迭相猜忌，五子皆不以壽終。

translations.literal: By his later years father, sons, and brothers successively suspected one another, and none of the five sons died a natural death.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years father, sons, and brothers turned on one another in suspicion, and none of the five sons died a natural death.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：昔辛伯諗周桓公曰：「內寵並後，外寵貳政，嬖子配嫡，大都偶國，亂之本也。」

translations.literal: Your subject Guang says: Formerly Xin Bo admonished Duke Huan of Zhou, saying: "Favorites rivaling the empress, outside favorites dividing power, beloved sons matching the legitimate heir, great cities matching the state—these are the roots of disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant Guang observes: Long ago Xin Bo warned Duke Huan of Zhou, saying, "When inner favorites rival the empress, outside favorites divide power, beloved sons match the heir, and great cities rival the throne—that is the root of disorder."

sentences.zh: 人主誠能慎此四者，亂何自生哉！

translations.literal: If a ruler can truly be careful of these four things, how would disorder arise of itself!
translations.idiomatic: If a ruler truly guards against these four things, how can disorder arise!

sentences.zh: 隋高祖徒知嫡庶之多爭，孤弱之易搖，曾不知勢鈞位逼，雖同產至親，不能無相傾奪。

translations.literal: Sui Emperor Gaozu knew only that legitimate and secondary sons contend much and that the isolated and weak are easily shaken, yet did not know that when power and position press equally, even brothers of the same womb cannot avoid mutual overthrow and seizure.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Sui knew only that legitimate and illegitimate sons fight and that the weak are easily toppled; he never understood that when power and position are equal, even full brothers of the same womb cannot help overthrowing one another.

sentences.zh: 考諸辛伯之言，得其一而失其三乎！

translations.literal: Examining Xin Bo's words, did he grasp one and lose three!
translations.idiomatic: Measured against Xin Bo's warning, he grasped one point and missed three!

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己卯，葬文皇帝於太陵，廟號高祖，與文獻皇后同墳異穴。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day jimao: Emperor Wen was buried at Tailang; temple name Gaozu, sharing a mound but separate chambers with Empress Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on day jimao, Emperor Wen was buried at Tailang with the temple name Gaozu, in the same mound as Empress Wenxian but in a separate chamber.

sentences.zh: 詔除婦人及奴婢、部曲之課，男子二十二成丁。

translations.literal: An edict abolished levies on women, slaves, and retainers, and set twenty-two as the age of male maturity for corvée.
translations.idiomatic: An edict abolished taxes on women, slaves, and household retainers and fixed the age of male adulthood for corvée at twenty-two.

sentences.zh: 章仇太翼言於帝曰：「陛下木命，雍州為破木之沖，不可久居。

translations.literal: Zhangqiu Taiyi said to the emperor: "Your Majesty's fate is Wood; Yongzhou is the clash that breaks Wood—you cannot dwell there long.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangqiu Taiyi told the emperor, "Your Majesty's fate element is Wood, and Yongzhou is the clash that shatters Wood—you cannot remain there long.

sentences.zh: 又讖云：『修治洛陽還晉家。』」

translations.literal: Moreover a prophecy says: 'Repair Luoyang and the Jin house returns.'"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover a prophecy says, 'Repair Luoyang and the house of Jin will return.'"

sentences.zh: 帝深以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply considered it so."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply convinced.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙未，幸洛陽，留晉王昭守長安。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day yiwei: he visited Luoyang and left Prince Jin Yang Zhao to guard Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on day yiwei, he proceeded to Luoyang and left Prince Jin Yang Zhao to guard Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 楊素以功拜其子萬石、仁行、侄玄挺為儀同三司，賚物五萬段，綺羅千匹，諒妓妾二十人。

translations.literal: Yang Su for his merit had his sons Wanshi and Renxing and his nephew Xuanting appointed Senior General of the Third Rank, bestowed fifty thousand bolts of goods, a thousand bolts of silk gauze, and twenty singing girls and concubines from Liang.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit Yang Su had his sons Wanshi and Renxing and his nephew Xuanting made Senior Generals of the Third Rank, and was given fifty thousand bolts of goods, a thousand bolts of silk gauze, and twenty of Liang's concubines.

sentences.zh: 丙申，發丁男數十萬掘塹，自龍門東接長平、汲郡，抵臨清關，渡河至浚儀、襄城，達於上洛，以置關防。

translations.literal: Day bingshen: several hundred thousand adult males were mobilized to dig ditches from Longmen east connecting Changping and Jijun, reaching Linqing Pass, crossing the river to Junyi and Xiangcheng, extending to Shangluo, to establish frontier defenses.
translations.idiomatic: On day bingshen several hundred thousand men were mobilized to dig defensive ditches from Longmen east through Changping and Jijun to Linqing Pass, then across the river to Junyi and Xiangcheng and on to Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 壬子，陳叔寶卒；

translations.literal: Day renzi: Chen Shubao died.
translations.idiomatic: On day renzi Chen Shubao died.

sentences.zh: 贈大將軍、長城縣公，謚曰煬。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand General and Duke of Changcheng County, posthumous name Yang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand General and Duke of Changcheng County with the posthumous name Yang.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，下詔於伊洛建東京，仍曰：「宮室之制，本以便生，今所營構，務從儉約。」

translations.literal: Day guichou: an edict was issued to build the Eastern Capital at Yiluo, stating: "The system of palaces was originally for convenience in living; what is now constructed must follow frugality and restraint."
translations.idiomatic: On day guichou an edict ordered the Eastern Capital built at Yiluo, stating, "Palaces exist for the convenience of living; what we build now must be frugal and restrained."

sentences.zh: 蜀王秀之得罪也，右衛大將軍元冑坐與交通除名，久不得調。

translations.literal: When Prince Shu Yang Xiu was punished, Right Guard General Yuan Zhou was struck from the registers for communicating with him and long could not be reassigned.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Shu Yang Xiu fell from favor, Right Guard General Yuan Zhou was struck from the registers for associating with him and went long without a new post.

sentences.zh: 時慈州刺史上官政坐事徙嶺南，將軍丘和以蒲州失守除名，冑與和有舊，酒酣，謂和曰：「上官政，壯士也，今徙嶺表，得無大事乎！」

translations.literal: At that time Shangguan Zheng, governor of Cizhou, was banished to Lingnan for an offense; General Qiu He was struck from the registers for losing Puzhou. Zhou and He were old friends; when drunk Zhou said to He: "Shangguan Zheng is a stalwart man—now exiled beyond the ranges, might there not be great trouble!"
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Zheng, governor of Cizhou, had been banished to Lingnan; Qiu He had been struck from the registers for losing Puzhou. Zhou and He were old friends, and when drunk Zhou said to He, "Shangguan Zheng is a formidable man—sent to the far south, might he not raise great trouble!

sentences.zh: 因自拊腹曰：「若是公者，不徒然矣。」

translations.literal: He thereupon slapped his belly and said: "If it were this gentleman, it would not be in vain."
translations.idiomatic: He slapped his belly and added, "A man like that would not sit idle."

sentences.zh: 和奏之，冑竟坐死。

translations.literal: He reported this; Zhou in the end was punished with death.
translations.idiomatic: He reported this, and Zhou was executed.

sentences.zh: 於是征政為驍衛將軍，以和為代州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zheng was summoned as general of the Martial Guard and He was made governor of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was then recalled as general of the Martial Guard and He was made governor of Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 煬皇帝上之上

translations.literal: Emperor Yang, Part One, Upper
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang, Part One, Upper

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬辰朔，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day renchen on the new moon: amnesty for all under Heaven and change of reign title.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month, day renchen, an amnesty was proclaimed and the reign title was changed.

sentences.zh: 立妃蕭氏為皇后。

translations.literal: The consort of the Xiao clan was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xiao was made empress.

sentences.zh: 廢諸州總管府。

translations.literal: All prefectural governor-general offices were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: All prefectural governor-general offices were abolished.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，立晉王昭為皇太子。

translations.literal: Day bingchen: Prince Jin Yang Zhao was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On day bingchen Prince Jin Yang Zhao was made crown prince.

sentences.zh: 高祖之末，群臣有言林邑多奇寶者。

translations.literal: At the end of Gaozu's reign ministers said that Linyi had many rare treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Gaozu's reign ministers reported that Linyi held many rare treasures.

sentences.zh: 時天下無事，劉方新平交州，乃授方驩州道行軍總管，經略林邑。

translations.literal: The empire was at peace; Liu Fang had newly pacified Jiaozhou, and Fang was appointed campaign commander of the Huanzhou circuit to operate against Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was at peace and Liu Fang had just pacified Jiaozhou; Fang was made campaign commander on the Huanzhou front to subdue Linyi.

sentences.zh: 方遣欽州刺史寧長真等以步騎萬餘出越裳，方親帥大將軍張愻等以舟師出比景，是月，軍至海口。

translations.literal: Fang sent Ning Changzhen, governor of Qinzhou, and others with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry out through Zoulang; Fang personally led Grand General Zhang Xun and others with a fleet out from Bijing. That month the army reached Haikou.
translations.idiomatic: Fang sent Ning Changzhen, governor of Qinzhou, with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry through Zoulang, while he personally led Grand General Zhang Xun and a fleet from Bijing. That month the army reached the coast.

sentences.zh: 二月，戊辰，敕有司大陳金寶、器物、錦彩、車馬，引楊素及諸將討漢王諒有功者立於前，使奇章公牛弘宣詔，稱揚功伐，賜賚各有差。

translations.literal: Second month, day wuchen: an edict ordered the offices to display gold treasures, utensils, brocades, and carriages in great array, led Yang Su and the generals who had merit in suppressing Prince Han Yang Liang to stand before them, and had Niuzhang Gongyang Hong proclaim the edict, praising their achievements, with rewards differing in degree.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on day wuchen, the emperor ordered gold, vessels, brocades, and carriages displayed in state, summoned Yang Su and the generals who had suppressed Prince Han, and had Gongyang Hong of Niuzhang read the edict praising their achievements and distributing rewards.

sentences.zh: 素等再拜舞蹈而出。

translations.literal: Su and the others bowed twice, performed the dance of obeisance, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Su and the others bowed, performed the court dance, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 己卯，以素為尚書令。

translations.literal: Day jimao: Su was made Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On day jimao Su was appointed Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 詔天下公除，惟帝服淺色黃衫、鐵裝帶。

translations.literal: An edict ordered public mourning throughout the empire; only the emperor wore a light-colored yellow shirt and iron-belt fittings.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered public mourning throughout the empire; only the emperor wore a pale yellow shirt and iron belt fittings.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁未，詔楊素與納言楊達、將作大匠宇文愷營建東京，每月役丁二百萬人，徙洛州郭內居民及諸州富商大賈數萬戶以實之。

translations.literal: Third month, day dingwei: an edict ordered Yang Su, together with Palace Counselor Yang Da and Master of Works Yuwen Kai, to build the Eastern Capital, with two million corvée laborers each month, moving residents within Luozhou's walls and tens of thousands of wealthy merchant households from various prefectures to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on day dingwei, Yang Su, Palace Counselor Yang Da, and Master of Works Yuwen Kai were ordered to build the Eastern Capital with two million corvée laborers a month, and tens of thousands of Luoyang residents and wealthy merchants from across the empire were moved in to populate it.

sentences.zh: 廢二崤道，開菱冊道。

translations.literal: The two Xia roads were abandoned and the Lingce road was opened.
translations.idiomatic: The two Xia roads were abandoned and the Lingce road was opened.

sentences.zh: 戊申，詔曰：「聽采輿頌，謀及庶民，故能審刑政之得失；

translations.literal: Day wushen: an edict said: "By listening to cart songs and popular praise and taking counsel even with commoners, one can examine the gains and losses of punishments and government.
translations.idiomatic: On day wushen an edict declared, "By heeding folk songs and consulting commoners, a ruler can judge whether justice and government succeed or fail.

sentences.zh: 今將巡歷淮、海，觀省風俗。」

translations.literal: Now I shall tour the Huai and sea regions and observe local customs."
translations.idiomatic: I shall now tour the Huai and coastal regions and observe local customs."

sentences.zh: 敕宇文愷與內史舍人封德彝等營顯仁宮。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yuwen Kai and Palace Secretary Feng Deyi and others to build Xianren Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Kai, Palace Secretary Feng Deyi, and others were ordered to build Xianren Palace.

sentences.zh: 南接皁澗，北跨洛濱。

translations.literal: South it joined the Zao Stream; north it spanned the Luo bank.
translations.idiomatic: It stretched south to the Zao Stream and north across the Luo embankment.

sentences.zh: 發大江之南、五嶺以北奇材異石，輸之洛陽；

translations.literal: Rare timbers and strange stones south of the Great River and north of the Five Ranges were mobilized and transported to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Exotic timbers and stones from south of the Yangzi and north of the Five Ranges were hauled to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 又求海內嘉木異草，珍禽奇獸，以實園苑。

translations.literal: Fine trees and strange plants, rare birds and exotic beasts from within the seas were also sought to fill the parks.
translations.idiomatic: Fine trees, rare plants, exotic birds, and strange beasts from across the empire were gathered to stock the parks.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，命尚書右丞皇甫議發河南、淮北諸郡民，前後百餘萬，開通濟渠。

translations.literal: Day xinhai: Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Huangfu Yi was ordered to mobilize the people of Henan and north-of-Huai prefectures, more than a million in all over time, to open the Tongji Canal.
translations.idiomatic: On day xinhai Huangfu Yi, Right Vice Director, was ordered to mobilize more than a million people from Henan and the Huai north to dig the Tongji Canal.

sentences.zh: 自西苑引谷、洛水達於河；

translations.literal: From the Western Park the Gu and Luo waters were led to reach the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: From the Western Park the Gu and Luo rivers were channeled to the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 復自板渚引河歷滎澤入汴；

translations.literal: Again from Banzhu the river was led through Xingze into the Bian.
translations.idiomatic: From Banzhu the Yellow River was led through Xingze into the Bian.

sentences.zh: 又自大梁之東引汴水入泗，達於淮；

translations.literal: Again from east of Daliang the Bian water was led into the Si, reaching the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: East of Daliang the Bian was channeled into the Si and on to the Huai.

sentences.zh: 又發淮南民十餘萬開邗溝，自山陽至楊子入江。

translations.literal: More than a hundred thousand Huainan people were mobilized to open the Hangou Canal from Shanyang to Yangzi entering the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred thousand Huainan laborers dug the Hangou Canal from Shanyang to Yangzi on the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 渠廣四十步，渠旁皆築御道，樹以柳；

translations.literal: The canal was forty paces wide; imperial roads were built on both banks and willows planted.
translations.idiomatic: The canal was forty paces wide, with imperial roads and willows on both banks.

sentences.zh: 自長安至江都，置離宮四十餘所。

translations.literal: From Chang'an to Jiangdu more than forty detached palaces were established.
translations.idiomatic: More than forty detached palaces were built from Chang'an to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 庚申，遣黃門侍郎王弘等往江南造龍舟及雜船數萬艘。

translations.literal: Day gengshen: Yellow Gate Attendant Wang Hong and others were sent to Jiangnan to build dragon boats and miscellaneous vessels numbering tens of thousands.
