translations.idiomatic: On day gengshen Wang Hong, Yellow Gate Attendant, and others were sent to Jiangnan to build dragon boats and tens of thousands of other vessels.

sentences.zh: 東京官吏督役嚴急，役丁死者什四五，所司以車載死丁，東至城皋，北至河陽，相望於道。

translations.literal: Officials of the Eastern Capital supervised labor harshly and urgently; forty or fifty percent of the corvée laborers died. The responsible offices loaded the dead on carts—from east to Chenggao, north to Heyang, they could be seen facing one another along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Capital officials drove the laborers mercilessly; forty or fifty percent died. Carts bearing the dead stretched from Chenggao in the east to Heyang in the north, one after another along the roads.

sentences.zh: 又作天經宮於東京，四時祭高祖。

translations.literal: The Tianjing Palace was also built in the Eastern Capital, with seasonal sacrifices to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: The Tianjing Palace was also built in the Eastern Capital for seasonal sacrifices to Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 林邑王梵志遣兵守險，劉方擊走之。

translations.literal: King Fan Zhi of Linyi sent troops to hold the passes; Liu Fang attacked and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: King Fan Zhi of Linyi sent troops to hold the passes; Liu Fang drove them off.

sentences.zh: 師渡闍黎江，林邑兵乘巨像，四面而至。

translations.literal: The army crossed the Zhanli River; Linyi troops rode great elephants and came from all sides.
translations.idiomatic: The army crossed the Zhanli River; Linyi forces advanced on war elephants from every side.

sentences.zh: 方戰不利，乃多掘小坑，草覆其上，以兵挑之，既戰，偽北；

translations.literal: Fang's battle went poorly; he dug many small pits, covered them with grass, provoked the enemy with troops, and after joining battle feigned retreat.
translations.idiomatic: When the battle went badly Fang dug many small pits, covered them with grass, skirmished with the enemy, then feigned retreat.

sentences.zh: 林邑逐之，像多陷地顛躓，轉相驚駭，軍遂亂。

translations.literal: Linyi pursued; many elephants sank and stumbled in the ground, startling one another in turn, and the army fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi pursued; elephants stumbled into the pits, panicked one another, and their army collapsed into chaos.

sentences.zh: 方以弩射象，像卻走，蹂其陣，因以銳師繼之。

translations.literal: Fang shot the elephants with crossbows; the elephants turned and fled, trampling their own ranks, and he followed with crack troops.
translations.idiomatic: Fang shot the elephants with crossbows; they turned and fled, trampling their own lines, and he pressed the attack with elite troops.

sentences.zh: 林邑大敗，俘馘萬計。

translations.literal: Linyi was utterly defeated; captives and severed ears numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi was routed; captives and heads numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 方引兵追之，屢戰皆捷，過馬援銅柱南，八日至其國都。

translations.literal: Fang led troops in pursuit, winning repeated battles, passed south of Ma Yuan's bronze pillar, and in eight days reached their capital.
translations.idiomatic: Fang pursued, winning every engagement, passed south of Ma Yuan's bronze pillar, and reached their capital in eight days.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，梵志棄城走入海。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Fan Zhi abandoned the city and fled into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Fan Zhi abandoned the capital and fled overseas.

sentences.zh: 方入城，獲其廟主十八，皆鑄金為之；

translations.literal: Fang entered the city and obtained eighteen temple icons, all cast in gold.
translations.idiomatic: Fang entered the city and seized eighteen golden temple icons.

sentences.zh: 刻石紀功而還。

translations.literal: He carved stone to record his merit and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He carved a stone monument to his victory and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 士卒腫足，死者什四五。

translations.literal: Soldiers' feet swelled; forty or fifty percent died.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers' feet swelled with disease and forty or fifty percent died.

sentences.zh: 方亦得疾，卒於道。

translations.literal: Fang also fell ill and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Fang also fell ill and died on the march home.

sentences.zh: 初，尚書右丞李綱數以異議忤楊素及蘇威，素薦綱於高祖，以為方行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Earlier Right Vice Director Li Gang had repeatedly offended Yang Su and Su Wei with differing opinions. Su recommended Gang to Gaozu, and Gang was made Fang's campaign marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Gang, Right Vice Director, had repeatedly crossed Yang Su and Su Wei with dissenting views. Su recommended him to Gaozu, and Gang was made Liu Fang's campaign marshal.

sentences.zh: 方承素意，屈辱之，幾死。

translations.literal: Fang followed Su's intent, humiliated him, and he nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: Fang, doing Su's bidding, humiliated him nearly to death.

sentences.zh: 軍還，久不得調，威復遣綱詣南海應接林邑，久而不召。

translations.literal: When the army returned he long could not be reassigned; Wei again sent Gang to Nanhai to support Linyi operations, and for a long time did not summon him back.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he went long without reassignment; Wei sent him to Nanhai to support the Linyi operation and left him there for years without recall.

sentences.zh: 綱自歸奏事，威劾奏綱擅離所職，下吏案問；

translations.literal: Gang returned on his own to report affairs; Wei impeached him for leaving his post without authorization and had officials investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Gang returned on his own to report; Wei impeached him for abandoning his post and had him investigated.

sentences.zh: 會赦，免官，屏居於鄠。

translations.literal: An amnesty intervened; he was dismissed from office and lived in seclusion at E.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty spared his life but he was dismissed and lived in retirement at E.

sentences.zh: 五月，築西苑，週二百里；

translations.literal: Fifth month: the Western Park was built, two hundred li in circumference.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Western Park was built, two hundred li around.

sentences.zh: 其內為海，周十餘里；

translations.literal: Within it was a sea more than ten li around.
translations.idiomatic: Inside was an artificial sea more than ten li around.

sentences.zh: 為方丈、蓬萊、瀛洲諸山，高出水百餘尺，台觀宮殿，羅絡山上，向背如神。

translations.literal: Mountains of Fangzhang, Penglai, Yingzhou and others were made, rising more than a hundred feet above the water; terraces, towers, and palaces were arrayed on the mountains, facing and backing one another like divine works.
translations.idiomatic: Isles of Fangzhang, Penglai, and Yingzhou rose more than a hundred feet above the water, crowned with terraces and palaces facing one another like a divine landscape.

sentences.zh: 北有龍鱗渠，縈紆注海內。

translations.literal: North was the Dragon Scale Canal, winding and pouring into the inner sea.
translations.idiomatic: To the north the Dragon Scale Canal wound into the inner sea.

sentences.zh: 緣渠作十六院，門皆臨渠，每院以四品夫人主之，堂殿樓觀，窮極華麗。

translations.literal: Along the canal sixteen courtyards were built, all gates facing the canal; each courtyard was headed by a lady of fourth rank, with halls, towers, and pavilions of utmost splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen courtyards lined the canal, each gate opening on the water, each headed by a lady of fourth rank, with halls and towers of extravagant splendor.

sentences.zh: 宮樹秋冬凋落，則剪綵為華葉，綴於枝條，色渝則易以新者，常如陽春。

translations.literal: When palace trees withered in autumn and winter, colored silks were cut into flowers and leaves and hung on the branches; when the colors faded they were replaced with new ones, ever like spring.
translations.idiomatic: When the trees shed their leaves in autumn and winter, silk flowers and leaves were hung on the branches and replaced when they faded, so the park was always in spring.

sentences.zh: 沼內亦剪綵為荷芰菱芡，乘輿游幸，則去冰而布之。

translations.literal: In the ponds colored silks were also cut into lotus, water chestnut, and gorgon plants; when the imperial carriage toured, the ice was removed and they were spread out.
translations.idiomatic: Silk lotus and water plants were laid on the ponds; when the emperor toured, the ice was broken and they were spread on the water.

sentences.zh: 十六院競以淆羞精麗相高，求市恩寵。

translations.literal: The sixteen courtyards competed in delicacies and refined fare to outdo one another, seeking to buy favor and grace.
translations.idiomatic: The sixteen courtyards vied in lavish feasts to win the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 上好以月夜從宮女數千騎游西苑，作《清夜遊曲》，於馬上奏之。

translations.literal: The emperor liked on moonlit nights to tour the Western Park with several thousand palace women on horseback, composing the tune "Clear Night Journey" and performing it on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved to ride through the Western Park on moonlit nights with thousands of palace women, composing the song "Clear Night Journey" and playing it from horseback.

sentences.zh: 帝待諸王恩薄，多所猜忌。

translations.literal: The emperor treated the princes with thin favor and much suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treated his brothers sparingly and suspected them constantly.

sentences.zh: 滕王綸、衛王集內自憂懼，呼術者問吉凶及章醮求福。

translations.literal: Prince Teng Yang Lun and Prince Wei Yang Ji inwardly worried and feared; they summoned technicians to ask fortune and misfortune and performed zhang jiao rites seeking blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Teng Yang Lun and Prince Wei Yang Ji, fearful within, consulted diviners and performed Daoist rites for protection.

sentences.zh: 或告其怨望咒詛，有司奏請誅之；

translations.literal: Someone reported their resentful looks and curses; the offices memorialized requesting execution.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported their resentment and curses; officials urged their execution.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙午，詔除名為民，徙邊郡。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day bingwu: an edict struck their names from the registers and banished them to frontier prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on day bingwu, an edict struck them from the registers and exiled them to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 綸，瓚之子；

translations.literal: Lun was the son of Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was a son of Yang Zan.

sentences.zh: 集，爽之子也。

translations.literal: Ji was the son of Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was a son of Yang Shuang.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬寅，上行幸江都，發顯仁宮，王弘遣龍舟奉迎。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day renyin: the emperor visited Jiangdu, departing from Xianren Palace; Wang Hong sent dragon boats to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on day renyin, the emperor set out for Jiangdu from Xianren Palace; Wang Hong sent dragon boats to meet him.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，上御小朱航，自漕渠出洛口，御龍舟。

translations.literal: Day yisi: the emperor boarded the small vermilion fleet, exited from the transport canal at Luokou, and boarded the dragon boat.
translations.idiomatic: On day yisi he boarded the small vermilion fleet, left through the canal at Luokou, and transferred to the dragon boat.

sentences.zh: 龍舟四重，高四十五十尺，長二百丈。

translations.literal: The dragon boat had four decks, was forty-five to fifty feet high, and two hundred zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: The dragon boat had four decks, stood forty-five zhang high, and was two hundred zhang long.

sentences.zh: 上重有正殿、內殿、東西朝堂，中二重有百二十房，皆飾以金玉，下重內侍處之。

translations.literal: The upper deck had the main hall, inner hall, and eastern and western audience halls; the middle two decks had one hundred twenty chambers, all adorned with gold and jade; the lower deck housed inner attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The top deck held the main hall, inner hall, and eastern and western audience halls; the middle two decks held one hundred twenty chambers adorned with gold and jade; eunuchs occupied the lower deck.

sentences.zh: 皇后乘翔□離舟，制度差小，而裝飾無異。

translations.literal: The empress rode the Xiang [character missing] Li boat, slightly smaller in scale but no different in ornament.
translations.idiomatic: The empress rode the Qingluan boat, somewhat smaller but equally lavish.

sentences.zh: 別有浮景九艘，三重，皆水殿也，。

translations.literal: Separately there were nine Floating Vista vessels, triple-decked, all water palaces.
translations.idiomatic: There were also nine triple-deck Floating Vista vessels, all floating palaces.

sentences.zh: 又有漾彩、朱鳥、蒼□離、白虎、玄武、飛羽、青鳧、陵波、五樓、道場、玄壇、板𦪙、黃篾等數千艘，後宮、諸王、公主、百官、僧、尼、道士、蕃客乘之，及載內外百司供奉之物，共用挽船士八萬餘人，其挽漾彩以上者九千餘人，謂之殿腳，皆以錦彩為袍。

translations.literal: There were also Yangcai, Vermilion Bird, Cang [character missing] Li, White Tiger, Black Warrior, Flying Plume, Green Duck, Wave-Cleaver, Five Towers, Dao Field, Mysterious Altar, Ban [character damaged], Yellow Bamboo, and others numbering several thousand vessels, ridden by the inner palace, princes, princesses, officials, monks, nuns, Daoist priests, and foreign guests, and carrying tribute goods of the hundred offices inside and outside; altogether more than eighty thousand boat haulers were used, of whom more than nine thousand hauled Yangcai and above—they were called Palace Feet and all wore brocade robes.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands more vessels—the Yangcai, Vermilion Bird, Cangli, White Tiger, Black Warrior, and many others—carried the inner palace, princes, princesses, officials, monks, nuns, Daoists, and foreign guests, along with supplies for every office. More than eighty thousand men hauled the boats; nine thousand of the elite haulers of the grandest vessels, called Palace Feet, wore brocade robes.

sentences.zh: 又有平乘、青龍、艨艟、艚艟、八棹、艇舸等數千艘，並十二衛兵乘之，並載兵器帳幕，兵士自引，不給夫。

translations.literal: There were also Pingsheng, Green Dragon, Mengchong, Zoucong, Eight-Oar, and Dingge vessels numbering several thousand, all ridden by the Twelve Guards, also carrying weapons and tent curtains, with soldiers hauling for themselves and no corvée labor supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of warships of the Twelve Guards—Pingsheng, Green Dragon, Mengchong, and others—carried weapons and tents, rowed by the soldiers themselves without corvée haulers.

sentences.zh: 舳艫相接二百餘里，照耀川陸，騎兵翊兩岸而行，旌旗蔽野。

translations.literal: Stern to prow connected for more than two hundred li, illuminating river and land; cavalry escorted along both banks, banners and flags covering the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: The fleet stretched stern to prow for more than two hundred li, lighting river and shore; cavalry rode both banks and banners blotted out the sky.

sentences.zh: 所過州縣，五百里內皆令獻食，多者一州至百轝，極水陸珍奇；

translations.literal: Every prefecture and county passed was ordered within five hundred li to present food; the most gave up to a hundred cartloads per prefecture, with land and water delicacies at the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Every county within five hundred li was ordered to supply food—some prefectures sent a hundred cartloads of the rarest delicacies by land and water.

sentences.zh: 後宮厭飫，將發之際，多棄埋之。

translations.literal: The inner palace grew surfeited; when about to depart they mostly abandoned and buried the food.
translations.idiomatic: The inner palace grew glutted; before departing they buried much of the food untouched.

sentences.zh: 契丹寇營州，詔通事謁者韋雲起護突厥兵討之，啟民可汗發騎二萬，受其處分。

translations.literal: The Khitan raided Yingzhou; an edict ordered Interpreter-Attendant Wei Yunqi to lead Turkic troops to suppress them; Qimin Khaghan sent twenty thousand horsemen under his command.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan raided Yingzhou; Wei Yunqi, Interpreter-Attendant, was ordered to lead Turkic troops against them, and Qimin Khaghan sent twenty thousand horsemen under his command.

sentences.zh: 雲起分為二十營，四道俱引，營相去一里，不得交雜，聞鼓聲而行，聞角聲而止，自非公使，勿得走馬，三令五申，擊鼓而發。

translations.literal: Yunqi divided them into twenty camps, four routes advancing together, camps one li apart without intermixing; on hearing drums they marched, on hearing horns they halted; unless on public business none might gallop; orders were repeated thrice and five times, and at the drum they set out.
translations.idiomatic: Yunqi divided them into twenty camps on four routes, one li apart, with strict discipline: march at the drum, halt at the horn, no galloping without orders. After repeated warnings they set out at the drum.

sentences.zh: 有紇干犯約，斬之，持首以徇。

translations.literal: A Heghan violated the rules; he was beheaded and the head displayed as warning.
translations.idiomatic: A Heghan soldier broke discipline; Yunqi beheaded him and displayed the head as a warning.

sentences.zh: 於是突厥將帥入謁，皆膝行股慄，莫敢仰視。

translations.literal: Thereupon Turkic generals and commanders came to audience, all crawling on knees and thighs trembling, none daring to look up.
translations.idiomatic: Turkic officers came to audience crawling on their knees, trembling, afraid to look up.

sentences.zh: 契丹本事突厥，情無猜忌。

translations.literal: The Khitan had long served the Turks and were without suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan had long been subject to the Turks and suspected nothing.

sentences.zh: 雲起既入其境，使突厥詐雲向柳城與高麗交易，敢漏洩事實者斬。

translations.literal: Once Yunqi had entered their territory he had the Turks pretend they were heading to Liucheng to trade with Goguryeo; whoever leaked the truth was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside Khitan territory Yunqi had the Turks pretend they were bound for Liucheng to trade with Goguryeo; anyone who revealed the truth was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 契丹不為備，去其營五十里，馳進襲之，盡獲其男女四萬口，殺其男子，以女子及畜產之半賜突厥，餘皆收之以歸。

translations.literal: The Khitan made no preparations; fifty li from their camp he charged in and raided them, capturing all forty thousand men and women, killing the men, giving half the women and livestock to the Turks, and taking the rest back.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan were unprepared. Fifty li from their camp Yunqi charged in and captured forty thousand men and women, killed the men, gave half the women and livestock to the Turks, and took the rest home.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，集百官曰：「雲起用突厥平契丹，才兼文武，朕今自舉之。」

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, gathered the hundred officials, and said: "Yunqi used Turks to pacify the Khitan—talent combining civil and military; I now promote him myself."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and told the officials, "Yunqi used Turks to crush the Khitan—talent in both civil and military affairs. I promote him myself."

sentences.zh: 擢為治書侍御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 初，西突厥阿波可汗為葉護可汗所虜，國人立鞅素特勒之子，是為泥利可汗。

translations.literal: Earlier, Apo Khaghan of the Western Turks was captured by Yehu Khaghan; the people enthroned the son of Yangsu Tegin, who was Nili Khaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Apo Khaghan of the Western Turks was captured by Yehu Khaghan; the people enthroned Yangsu Tegin's son as Nili Khaghan.

sentences.zh: 泥利卒，子達漫立，號處羅可汗。

translations.literal: When Nili died his son Damo was enthroned, styled Khaghan Chuluo.
translations.idiomatic: When Nili died his son Damo succeeded as Khaghan Chuluo.

sentences.zh: 其母向氏，本中國人，更嫁泥利之弟婆實特勒。

translations.literal: His mother Lady Xiang was originally a Chinese; she remarried Nili's younger brother Boshi Tegin.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Xiang, was originally Chinese; she remarried Nili's younger brother Boshi Tegin.

sentences.zh: 開皇末，婆實與向氏入朝，遇達頭之亂，遂留長安，捨於鴻臚寺。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaihuang, Boshi and Lady Xiang entered court; they encountered Tardu Khan's turmoil and remained in Chang'an, lodged at the Court of Diplomatic Reception.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaihuang era Boshi and Lady Xiang came to court; caught in Tardu Khan's upheaval, they stayed in Chang'an at the Court of Diplomatic Reception.

sentences.zh: 處羅多居烏孫故地，撫御失道，國人多叛，復為鐵勒所困。

translations.literal: Chuluo mostly dwelt in the old Wusun lands; his rule lost the way and many of the people rebelled; he was again beset by the Tiele.
translations.idiomatic: Chuluo mostly held the old Wusun lands but governed badly; many of his people rebelled, and the Tiele pressed him hard.

sentences.zh: 鐵勒者，匈奴之遺種，族類最多，有僕骨、同羅、契苾、薛延陀等部，其酋長皆號俟斤。

translations.literal: The Tiele were descendants of the Xiongnu, with the most numerous tribal groups, including Pugu, Tongluo, Qibi, Xueyantuo, and others; their chiefs were all styled irkin.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele were descendants of the Xiongnu, with many tribes including Pugu, Tongluo, Qibi, and Xueyantuo; their chiefs were called irkin.

sentences.zh: 族姓雖殊，通謂之鐵勒，大抵與突厥同俗，以寇抄為生，無大君長，分屬東、西兩突厥。

translations.literal: Though clan names differed, they were commonly called Tiele; broadly they shared Turkic customs, lived by raiding, had no great paramount chief, and were divided between the Eastern and Western Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Though their clans differed, all were called Tiele; they shared Turkic customs, lived by raiding, had no single paramount chief, and were split between the Eastern and Western Turks.

sentences.zh: 是歲，處羅引兵擊鐵勒諸部，厚稅其物，又猜忌薛延陀，恐其為變，集其酋長數百人，盡殺之。

translations.literal: That year Chuluo led troops to attack the Tiele tribes, heavily taxed their goods, and also suspected the Xueyantuo; fearing they would revolt, he gathered several hundred of their chiefs and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: That year Chuluo attacked the Tiele tribes, taxed them heavily, and fearing the Xueyantuo might rebel, summoned several hundred of their chiefs and slaughtered them.

sentences.zh: 於是鐵勒皆叛，立俟利發俟斤契苾歌楞為莫何可汗，又立薛延陀俟斤字也咥為小可汗，與處羅戰，屢破之。

translations.literal: Thereupon all the Tiele rebelled, enthroned Irkin Qibi Geleng of the Irli tribe as Mohe Khaghan, and also enthroned Irkin Ziye of the Xueyantuo as lesser khaghan; they fought Chuluo and repeatedly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: All the Tiele rose in rebellion, made Qibi Geleng of the Irli tribe Mohe Khaghan, and Ziye of the Xueyantuo lesser khaghan; they fought Chuluo and beat him again and again.

sentences.zh: 莫何勇毅絕倫，甚得眾心，為鄰國所憚，伊吾、高昌、焉耆皆附之。

translations.literal: Mohe was brave and resolute beyond compare, greatly won the people's hearts, and was feared by neighboring states; Yiwu, Gaochang, and Yanqi all attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: Mohe was incomparably brave and won the people's loyalty; neighboring states feared him, and Yiwu, Gaochang, and Yanqi all submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛酉，東京成，進將作大匠宇文愷位開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day xinyou: the Eastern Capital was completed; Master of Works Yuwen Kai was advanced to Senior General of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on day xinyou, the Eastern Capital was completed and Yuwen Kai, Master of Works, was promoted to Senior General of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，遣十使並省州省。

translations.literal: Day dingmao: ten envoys were dispatched to merge and reduce prefectures and provinces.
translations.idiomatic: On day dingmao ten envoys were sent to consolidate prefectures and provinces.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙戌，詔吏部尚書牛弘等議定輿服、儀衛制度。

translations.literal: Second month, day bingxu: an edict ordered Minister of Personnel Niu Hong and others to deliberate and fix regulations for carriages, robes, and ceremonial guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on day bingxu, Niu Hong, Minister of Personnel, and others were ordered to draft regulations for carriages, robes, and ceremonial guards.

sentences.zh: 以開府儀同三司何稠為太府少卿，使之營造，送江都。

translations.literal: He Dou of Kaifeng, Senior General of the Third Rank, was made Vice Director of the Imperial Storehouse to oversee construction and send the results to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: He Dou, Senior General of the Third Rank, was made Vice Director of the Imperial Storehouse to oversee the work and ship everything to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 稠智思精巧，博覽圖籍，參會古今，多所損益；

translations.literal: Chou was clever and ingenious in mind, broadly read maps and records, compared past and present, and made many additions and subtractions.
translations.idiomatic: Chou was ingenious, widely read, and revised the ancient regulations to suit the present.

sentences.zh: 袞冕畫日、月、星、辰，皮弁用漆紗為之。

translations.literal: The ceremonial robes were painted with sun, moon, stars, and constellations; the leather cap was made of lacquered gauze.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial robes bore sun, moon, stars, and constellations; the leather caps were made of lacquered gauze.

sentences.zh: 又作黃麾三萬六千人仗，及輅輦車輿，皇后鹵簿，百官儀服，務為華盛，以稱上意。

translations.literal: He also made thirty-six thousand yellow-banner guard regalia, imperial carriages and palanquins, the empress's outer escort, and ceremonial dress for the hundred officials, striving for splendor to match the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: He also made thirty-six thousand yellow-banner guards, imperial carriages, the empress's escort, and ceremonial dress for all officials—everything as lavish as the emperor desired.

sentences.zh: 課州縣送羽毛，民求捕之，網羅被水陸，禽獸有堪氅毦之用者，殆無遺類。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties were levied to deliver feathers; the people sought to capture them; nets covered land and water; birds and beasts usable for feathered plumes were nearly exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures were ordered to supply feathers; people hunted land and water until almost every bird and beast fit for plumes was gone.

sentences.zh: 烏程有高樹，逾百尺，旁無附枝，上有鶴巢，民欲取之，不可上，乃伐其根；

translations.literal: In Wucheng was a tall tree exceeding a hundred feet with no side branches; a crane's nest was above; the people wished to take it but could not climb up, so they cut the roots.
translations.idiomatic: At Wucheng stood a tree over a hundred feet tall with a crane's nest atop it; unable to climb it, the people cut down the roots.

sentences.zh: 鶴恐殺其子，自拔氅毛投於地，時人或稱以為瑞，曰：「天子造羽儀，鳥獸自獻羽毛。」

translations.literal: The crane, fearing its young would be killed, plucked its own plumes and cast them to the ground; some at the time called it an auspice, saying: "The Son of Heaven makes feathered regalia, and birds and beasts offer feathers of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for its young, the crane plucked its own feathers and dropped them to the ground; some called it an omen that birds offered feathers for the emperor's regalia.

sentences.zh: 所役工十萬餘人，用金銀錢帛巨億計。

translations.literal: Laborers employed numbered more than a hundred thousand; gold, silver, cash, and silk used ran to hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred thousand laborers were employed at a cost of hundreds of millions in gold, silver, and silk.

sentences.zh: 帝每出遊幸，羽儀填街溢路，亙二十餘里。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went out on tour, feathered regalia filled and overflowed the streets for more than twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went abroad, his retinue filled the streets for more than twenty li.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚戌，上發江都，夏，四月，庚戌，自伊闕陳法駕，備千乘萬騎入東京。

translations.literal: Third month, day gengxu: the emperor departed Jiangdu. Summer, fourth month, day gengxu: from Yique he displayed the imperial procession with a thousand chariots and ten thousand riders and entered the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on day gengxu, he left Jiangdu. In summer, the fourth month, on day gengxu, he entered the Eastern Capital from Yique in full imperial procession with thousands of chariots and horsemen.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，御端門，大赦，免天下今年租賦。

translations.literal: Day xinhai: he held court at the Duan Gate, proclaimed a great amnesty, and remitted this year's rents and taxes throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: On day xinhai he held court at the Duan Gate, proclaimed a great amnesty, and remitted the year's rents and taxes empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 制五品以上文官乘車，在朝弁服，佩玉；

translations.literal: It was decreed that civil officials of fifth rank and above ride in carriages, wear court caps and robes in audience, and wear jade pendants.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials of fifth rank and above were required to ride in carriages, wear court dress in audience, and wear jade pendants.

sentences.zh: 武官馬加珂，戴幘，服褲褶。

translations.literal: Military officials had horses with trappings, wore headcloths, and wore trousers and short jackets.
translations.idiomatic: Military officials rode horses with trappings, wore headcloths, and dressed in trousers and short jackets.

sentences.zh: 文物之盛，近世莫及也。

translations.literal: "The splendor of ritual and regalia—recent ages could not match it."
translations.idiomatic: "The splendor of court ritual had not been matched in recent memory."

sentences.zh: 六月，壬子，以楊素為司徒，進封豫章王暕為齊王。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day renzi: Yang Su was made Minister of Education; Prince Yuzhang Yang Jian was advanced and enfeoffed as Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on day renzi, Yang Su was made Minister of Education and Prince Yuzhang Yang Jian was enfeoffed as Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，庚申，制百官不得計考增級，必有德行、功能灼然顯著者進擢之。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day gengshen: it was decreed that the hundred officials could not advance rank by routine annual evaluation; only those with virtue and conduct or merit clearly outstanding were to be promoted.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on day gengshen, officials were forbidden routine promotion by seniority; only those of clearly outstanding virtue or merit could advance.

sentences.zh: 帝頗惜名位，群臣當進職者，多令兼假而已；

translations.literal: The emperor was quite sparing of titles and posts; ministers who should have advanced in office were mostly given concurrent or acting appointments only.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hoarded titles and ranks; ministers due for promotion usually received only acting or concurrent appointments.

sentences.zh: 雖有闕員，留而不補。

translations.literal: Even when there were vacancies they were left unfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Even vacant posts were left unfilled.

sentences.zh: 時牛弘為吏部尚書，不得專行其職，別敕納言蘇威、左翊衛大將軍宇文述、左驍衛大將軍張瑾、內史侍郎虞世基、御史大夫裴蘊、黃門侍郎裴矩參掌選事，時人謂之「選曹七貴」。

translations.literal: At that time Niu Hong was Minister of Personnel but could not exercise his office alone; a separate edict ordered Palace Counselor Su Wei, Left Flank Guard General Yuwen Shu, Left Martial Guard General Zhang Jin, Palace Secretary Yu Shiji, Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun, and Yellow Gate Attendant Pei Ju to share control of selection affairs; people of the time called them the "Seven Nobles of the Selection Bureau."
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hong was Minister of Personnel but could not act alone; Su Wei, Yuwen Shu, Zhang Jin, Yu Shiji, Pei Yun, and Pei Ju were ordered to share appointments—the "Seven Nobles of the Selection Bureau."

sentences.zh: 雖七人同在坐，然與奪之筆，虞世基獨專之，受納賄賂，多者超越等倫，無者注色而已。

translations.literal: Though all seven sat together, the brush of grant and denial was monopolized by Yu Shiji alone; he accepted bribes—those who gave much leaped over ranks, those who gave nothing received only a note of their names.
translations.idiomatic: Though all seven sat together, Yu Shiji alone held the power of appointment; he took bribes—generous donors leaped over their peers, others received only a notation.

sentences.zh: 蘊，邃之從曾孫也。

translations.literal: Yun was the great-great-grandson of Sui on the collateral line.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yun was a collateral descendant of Pei Sui.

sentences.zh: 元德太子昭自長安來朝，數月，將還，欲乞少留；

translations.literal: Crown Prince Yuande Zhao came from Chang'an to court; after several months, when about to return, he wished to beg to stay a little longer.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yuande Zhao came from Chang'an to court; after several months, as he prepared to return, he begged to stay a little longer.

sentences.zh: 帝不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 拜請無數，體素肥，因致勞疾，甲戌，薨。

translations.literal: He bowed and begged countless times; his constitution was naturally stout, and he thereby fell into illness from distress; on day jiaxu he died.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded again and again; naturally heavyset, he fell ill from grief and died on day jiaxu.

sentences.zh: 帝哭之，數聲而止，尋奏聲伎，無異平日。

translations.literal: The emperor wept for him, stopped after a few cries, and soon had music and performers play as on ordinary days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept briefly, then soon had music played as on any ordinary day.

sentences.zh: 楚景武公楊素，雖有大功，特為帝所猜忌，外示殊禮，內情甚薄。

translations.literal: Duke Jingwu of Chu Yang Su, though he had great merit, was especially suspected by the emperor; outwardly shown special courtesy, inwardly treated very thinly.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Jingwu of Chu, Yang Su, though he had great merit, was especially distrusted by the emperor—honored in public, held in contempt in private.

sentences.zh: 太史言隋分野有大喪，乃徙素為楚公，意言楚與隋同分，欲以厭之。

translations.literal: The Director of Astral Service said the Sui asterism would suffer great mourning; Su was therefore transferred to be Duke of Chu, meaning that Chu and Sui shared the same asterism, intending to avert it.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Astral Service predicted great mourning for the Sui asterism; Su was made Duke of Chu, sharing Sui's asterism, to avert the omen.

sentences.zh: 素寢疾，帝每令名醫診候，賜以上藥，然密問醫者，恆恐不死。

translations.literal: Su lay ill in bed; the emperor repeatedly had famous physicians examine him and bestowed superior medicines, yet secretly asked the physicians, always fearing he would not die.
translations.idiomatic: When Su fell ill the emperor sent famous physicians and fine medicines, yet secretly asked whether Su would recover—always fearing he would not die.

sentences.zh: 素亦自知名位已極，不肯餌藥，亦不將慎，謂弟約曰：「我豈須更活邪！」

translations.literal: Su also knew his fame and position had reached the limit, refused to take medicine, and was not careful, saying to his younger brother Yue: "Do I still need to live!"
translations.idiomatic: Su knew his power had peaked, refused medicine, and told his brother Yue, "Why should I go on living!"

sentences.zh: 乙亥，素薨，贈太尉公、弘農等十郡太守，葬送甚盛。

translations.literal: Day yihai: Su died; he was posthumously made Duke of Grand Commandant and governor of ten commanderies including Hongnong; the funeral was very grand.
translations.idiomatic: On day yihai Su died; he was posthumously made Grand Commandant and governor of ten commanderies including Hongnong, with a lavish funeral.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛卯，封皇孫倓為燕王，侗為越王，侑為代王，皆昭之子也。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day xinmao: imperial grandsons Tan was enfeoffed as Prince of Yan, Tong as Prince of Yue, and You as Prince of Dai—all sons of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on day xinmao, grandsons Tan, Tong, and You—sons of Zhao—were enfeoffed as princes of Yan, Yue, and Dai.

sentences.zh: 九月，乙丑，立秦孝王子浩為秦王。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day yichou: Prince Xiao of Qin's son Hao was established as Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on day yichou, Prince Xiao of Qin's son Hao was made Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 帝以高祖末年，法令峻刻，冬，十月，詔改修律令。

translations.literal: The emperor, because in Gaozu's last years laws and orders were harsh and severe, in winter, tenth month, ordered revision of statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Gaozu's late laws too harsh, the emperor in winter, the tenth month, ordered a revision of the code.

sentences.zh: 置洛口倉於鞏東南原上，築倉城，周回二十餘里，穿三千窖，窖容八千石以還，置監官並鎮兵千人。

translations.literal: The Luokou granary was established on the plateau southeast of Gong; a granary city was built, more than twenty li in circuit, with three thousand cellars dug, each holding eight thousand shi or less, with supervising officials and a thousand garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Luokou granary was built on the plateau southeast of Gong—a walled complex twenty li around with three thousand cellars holding up to eight thousand shi each, guarded by officials and a thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 十二月，置回洛倉於洛陽北七里，倉城周回十里，穿三百窖。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: the Huiluo granary was established seven li north of Luoyang; the granary city was ten li in circuit with three hundred cellars dug.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Huiluo granary was built seven li north of Luoyang—a ten-li compound with three hundred cellars.

sentences.zh: 初，齊溫公之世，有魚龍、山車等戲，謂之散樂，周宣帝時，鄭譯奏征之。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the age of Duke Wen of Qi, there were entertainments of fish-dragons, mountain carts, and the like, called scattered music; in Emperor Xuandi of Zhou's time Zheng Yi memorialized to recruit them.
translations.idiomatic: In Duke Wen of Qi's day there were entertainments such as fish-dragons and mountain carts called scattered music; under Zhou Emperor Xuandi Zheng Yi had them recruited.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，命牛弘定樂，非正聲清商及九部四舞之色，悉放遣之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication he ordered Niu Hong to fix the music; all that were not orthodox tones, pure shang modes, or the colors of the nine departments and four dances were dismissed and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne he ordered Niu Hong to regulate music and dismissed all performers outside orthodox court music.

sentences.zh: 帝以啟民可汗將入朝，欲以富樂誇之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Qimin Khaghan was about to enter court, wished to dazzle him with rich music.
translations.idiomatic: With Qimin Khaghan about to visit court, the emperor wished to dazzle him with lavish entertainments.

sentences.zh: 太常少卿裴蘊希旨，奏括天下周、齊、梁、陳樂家子弟皆為樂戶；

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrifices Pei Yun, following the emperor's intent, memorialized to register all musician families' sons and younger brothers of Zhou, Qi, Liang, and Chen throughout the empire as music households.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yun, Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrifices, following the emperor's wish, registered all musician families from the former Zhou, Qi, Liang, and Chen as music households.

sentences.zh: 其六品以下至庶人，有善音樂者，皆直太常。

translations.literal: Those from sixth rank down to commoners who were skilled in music were all assigned to the Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone from sixth rank down to commoners skilled in music was assigned to the Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是四方散樂，大集東京，閱之於芳華苑積翠池側。

translations.literal: Thereupon scattered music from all directions was greatly gathered at the Eastern Capital and reviewed beside the Accumulated Emerald Pool in the Garden of Flowering Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Scattered entertainers from across the empire were gathered at the Eastern Capital and performed beside the Accumulated Emerald Pool in the Garden of Flowering Splendor.

sentences.zh: 有捨利獸先來跳躍，激水滿衢，黿鼉、龜鱉、水人、蟲魚，遍覆於地。

translations.literal: First came a shari beast leaping and jumping, churning water to fill the streets; soft-shelled turtles, tortoises, water men, insects, and fish covered the ground everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: First a shari beast leaped about, flooding the streets with water and covering the ground with turtles, fish, and costumed water creatures.

sentences.zh: 又有鯨魚噴霧翳日，倏忽化成黃龍，長七八丈。

translations.literal: There was also a whale spouting mist that blotted the sun, suddenly transforming into a yellow dragon seven or eight zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: A whale spouted mist that blotted out the sun, then suddenly became a yellow dragon seven or eight zhang long.

sentences.zh: 又二人戴竿，上有舞者，焱□然騰過，左右易處。

translations.literal: Again two men wore poles on their heads with dancers above, who in a burst of flame leaped over and changed places left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Two men bore poles with dancers atop who leaped blazing from one to the other.

sentences.zh: 又有神鰲負山，幻人吐火，千變萬化。

translations.literal: There was also a divine ao tortoise bearing a mountain, illusionists spitting fire—thousands of changes and ten thousands of transformations.
translations.idiomatic: A divine tortoise bore a mountain; illusionists spat fire—in endless transformations.

sentences.zh: 伎人皆衣錦繡繒彩，舞者鳴環珮，綴花毦；

translations.literal: Performers all wore brocade and colored silks; dancers sounded rings and pendants and were adorned with flowered plumes.
translations.idiomatic: Performers wore brocades and silks; dancers jingled with rings and pendants and wore flowered plumes.

sentences.zh: 課京兆、河南制其衣，兩京錦彩為之空竭。

translations.literal: Jingzhao and Henan were levied to make their garments; brocades and silks in the two capitals were exhausted for it.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao and Henan were ordered to supply their costumes until both capitals' brocades were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 帝多制艷篇，令樂正白明達造新聲播之，音極哀怨。

translations.literal: The emperor composed many sensuous lyrics and ordered Music Director Bai Mingda to create new tunes to spread them, the sound extremely plaintive and sorrowful.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote many sensuous lyrics and had Music Director Bai Mingda compose new tunes of heartbreaking melancholy.

sentences.zh: 帝甚悅，謂明達曰：「齊氏偏隅，樂工曹妙達猶封王；

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and said to Mingda: "The Qi house was a corner realm, yet musician Cao Miaoda was still enfeoffed as king.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and told Mingda, "The petty Qi state enfeoffed its musician Cao Miaoda as a king.

sentences.zh: 我今天下大同，方且貴汝，宜自修謹！」

translations.literal: I today have unified all under Heaven and am about to honor you—you should cultivate yourself with care!"
translations.idiomatic: I have unified the empire and mean to honor you—conduct yourself carefully!"

sentences.zh: 春，正月，朔旦，大陳文物。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, at dawn on the new moon, ritual regalia was displayed in great array.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, at dawn on the new moon of the first month, court ritual was displayed in full splendor.

sentences.zh: 時突厥啟民可汗入朝，見而慕之，請襲冠帶，帝不許。

translations.literal: At that time Qimin Khaghan of the Turks entered court; seeing it he admired it and requested to adopt caps and belts; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Qimin Khaghan of the Turks was at court; admiring the display, he asked to adopt Chinese dress, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 明日，又帥其屬上表固請，帝大悅，謂牛弘等曰：「今衣冠大備，致單于解辮，卿等功也。」

translations.literal: The next day he again led his followers in a memorial firmly requesting it; the emperor was greatly pleased and said to Niu Hong and others: "Now caps and robes are fully prepared, causing the Single Leader to undo his braids—this is your merit."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he and his followers petitioned again; the emperor was delighted and told Niu Hong and others, "Our ritual is complete enough to make the khaghan cut his braids—this is your achievement."

sentences.zh: 各賜帛甚厚。

translations.literal: Each was bestowed very thick gifts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Each received a generous gift of silk.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛亥，帝還長安。

translations.literal: Third month, day xinhai: the emperor returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on day xinhai, the emperor returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，帝使羽騎尉朱寬入海求訪異俗，至流求國而還。

translations.literal: Day guichou: the emperor sent Feathered Cavalry Commandant Zhu Kuan to enter the sea seeking strange customs, reaching the state of Liuqiu and returning.
translations.idiomatic: On day guichou the emperor sent Zhu Kuan, Feathered Cavalry Commandant, to sea in search of foreign lands; he reached Liuqiu and returned.

sentences.zh: 初，雲定興、閻毘坐媚事太子勇，與妻子皆沒官為奴婢。

translations.literal: Earlier Yun Dingxing and Yan Pi were punished for fawning on Crown Prince Yong; with their wives and children they were all confiscated as government slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yun Dingxing and Yan Pi had been enslaved for currying favor with Crown Prince Yong.

sentences.zh: 上即位，多所營造，聞其有巧思，召之，使典其事，以毘為朝請郎。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne he undertook many constructions; hearing of their ingenuity he summoned them to oversee the affairs, and made Pi a Court Gentleman for Imperial Audience.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne he summoned them for their ingenuity to oversee construction and made Pi a Court Gentleman for Imperial Audience.

sentences.zh: 時宇文述用事，定興以明珠絡帳賂述，並以奇服新聲求媚於求；

translations.literal: At that time Yuwen Shu held power; Dingxing bribed Shu with pearl-net curtains and also sought favor with rare garments and new music.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shu was in power; Dingxing bribed him with pearl curtains and rare clothes and music.

sentences.zh: 述大喜，兄事之。

translations.literal: Shu was greatly pleased and treated him as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was delighted and treated him like an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 上將有事四夷，大造兵器，述薦定興可使監造，上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to undertake affairs with the four barbarians and greatly made weapons; Shu recommended Dingxing to supervise manufacture, and the emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor prepared for campaigns abroad and mass-produced arms, Shu recommended Dingxing to supervise manufacture, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 述謂定興曰：「兄所作器仗，併合上心，而不得官者，為長寧兄弟猶未死耳。」

translations.literal: Shu said to Dingxing: "The weapons elder brother makes all suit the emperor's mind, yet you receive no office because the Changning brothers are still not dead."
translations.idiomatic: Shu told Dingxing, "Your weapons please the emperor, but you get no rank because the Changning brothers still live."

sentences.zh: 定興曰：「此無用物，何不勸上殺之。」

translations.literal: Dingxing said: "These useless creatures—why not urge the emperor to kill them."
translations.idiomatic: Dingxing said, "Those useless men—why not urge the emperor to kill them?"

sentences.zh: 述因奏：「房陵諸子年並成立，今欲興兵征討，若使之從駕，則守掌為難；

translations.literal: Shu thereupon memorialized: "The sons at Fangling are all grown; now wishing to raise troops for campaigns, if they are made to follow the imperial procession, guarding them will be difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Shu memorialized, "The sons at Fangling are grown men; if they accompany the campaign they will be hard to guard.

sentences.zh: 若留於一處，又恐不可。

translations.literal: If left in one place, again there is fear it will not do.
translations.idiomatic: If left in one place, that is also dangerous.

sentences.zh: 進退無用，請早處分。」

translations.literal: Advancing or holding them is useless; I request early disposition."
translations.idiomatic: They are useless either way—dispose of them soon."

sentences.zh: 帝然之，乃鴆殺長寧王儼，分徙其七弟於嶺表，仍遣間使於路盡殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved; thereupon Prince Changning Yang Yan was killed with poisoned wine, his seven younger brothers were separately exiled beyond the ranges, and secret envoys were still sent on the road to kill them all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed; Prince Changning Yang Yan was poisoned, his seven brothers exiled to Lingnan, and secret agents killed them on the road.

sentences.zh: 襄城王恪之妃柳氏自殺以從恪。

translations.literal: Lady Liu, consort of Prince Xiangcheng Yang Ke, killed herself to follow Ke.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu, consort of Prince Xiangcheng Yang Ke, killed herself to follow her husband.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚辰，下詔欲安輯河北，巡省趙、魏。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day gengchen: an edict was issued wishing to pacify and settle Hebei and tour and inspect Zhao and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on day gengchen, an edict announced a tour to pacify Hebei and inspect Zhao and Wei.

sentences.zh: 牛弘等造新律成，凡十八篇，謂之《大業律》；

translations.literal: Niu Hong and others completed the new statutes, eighteen sections in all, called the Daye Code.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hong and others completed the new code in eighteen sections, called the Daye Code.

sentences.zh: 甲申，始頒行之。

translations.literal: Day jiashen: it was first promulgated and put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: On day jiashen it was promulgated.

sentences.zh: 民久厭嚴刻，喜於寬政。

translations.literal: The people had long wearied of harsh severity and rejoiced in lenient government.
translations.idiomatic: The people, long weary of harsh laws, rejoiced at the leniency.

sentences.zh: 其後征役繁興，民不堪命。

translations.literal: Afterward corvée and campaigns arose frequently and the people could not bear the commands.
translations.idiomatic: Soon corvée and campaigns multiplied until the people could not endure it.

sentences.zh: 有司臨時迫脅以求濟事，不復用律令矣。

translations.literal: The offices at the time coerced and pressed temporarily to accomplish affairs and no longer used statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Offices coerced people as expedience required, and the code fell into disuse.

sentences.zh: 旅騎尉劉炫預修律令，弘嘗從容問炫曰：「《周禮》士多而府史少，今令史百倍於前，減則不濟，其故何也？」

translations.literal: Cavalry Commandant Liu Xuan took part in revising the statutes; Hong once casually asked Xuan: "In the Rites of Zhou there were many gentlemen and few clerks; today clerks are a hundred times those before—reduce them and affairs fail; what is the reason?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan, Cavalry Commandant, had helped revise the code; Hong once asked him casually, "The Rites of Zhou had many gentlemen and few clerks; today clerks are a hundred times more numerous—cut them and work stops. Why?"

sentences.zh: 炫曰：「古人委任責成，歲終考其殿最，案不重校，文不繁悉，府史之任，掌要目而已。

translations.literal: Xuan said: "The ancients entrusted responsibility and demanded results; at year's end they examined best and worst; cases were not double-checked, documents were not elaborate and detailed—the clerk's charge was only to keep main headings.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan said, "The ancients delegated authority and judged results at year's end; records were not double-checked or endlessly detailed—clerks kept only the main headings.

sentences.zh: 今之文簿，恆慮覆治，若鍛煉不密，則萬里追證百年舊案。

translations.literal: Today's documents always fear re-examination; if forging is not tight, cases a hundred years old are pursued for proof ten thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: Today every document fears review; if a case is not ironclad, proof is chased ten thousand li for cases a century old.

sentences.zh: 故諺云：『老吏抱案死。』

translations.literal: Therefore the proverb says: 'An old clerk dies clutching his files.'"
translations.idiomatic: Hence the proverb: 'An old clerk dies clutching his files.'"

sentences.zh: 事繁政弊，職此之由也。」

translations.literal: Affairs numerous and government decayed—this is the cause."
translations.idiomatic: Bloated paperwork is the root of bad government.

sentences.zh: 弘曰：「魏、齊之時，令史從容而已，今則不遑寧處，何故？」

translations.literal: Hong said: "In Wei and Qi times clerks were at ease; today they have no leisure to rest—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Hong asked, "Under Wei and Qi clerks had leisure; today they never rest—why?"

sentences.zh: 炫曰：「往者州唯置綱紀，郡置守、丞，縣置令而已。

translations.literal: Xuan said: "Formerly a province set only an inspector; a commandery set a governor and aide; a county set only a magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan said, "Formerly a province had only an inspector, a commandery a governor and aide, a county only a magistrate.

sentences.zh: 其餘具僚則長官自辟，受詔赴任，每州不過數十。

translations.literal: The rest of the full staff the chief official recruited himself; receiving the edict they took up office—each province had no more than several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Other staff were recruited by the chief; each province had only a few dozen officials.

sentences.zh: 今則不然，大小之官，悉由吏部，纖介之跡，皆屬考功。

translations.literal: Today it is not so—all offices great and small come from the Ministry of Personnel, and the slightest trace belongs to the evaluation of merit.
translations.idiomatic: Today every post, great or small, comes from the Ministry of Personnel, and every detail is tracked by the evaluation office.

sentences.zh: 省官不如省事，官事不省而望從容，其可得乎！」

translations.literal: Reducing officials is not as good as reducing affairs; affairs not reduced yet hoping for leisure—how can it be obtained!"
translations.idiomatic: Cutting officials is useless without cutting paperwork—how can clerks ever rest!"

sentences.zh: 弘善其言而不能用。

translations.literal: Hong approved his words but could not apply them."
translations.idiomatic: Hong agreed but could not act on it."

sentences.zh: 壬辰，改州為郡；

translations.literal: Day renchen: prefectures were changed to commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: On day renchen prefectures were renamed commanderies.

sentences.zh: 改度量權衡，並依古式。

translations.literal: Weights, measures, and balances were changed, all following ancient models.
translations.idiomatic: Weights, measures, and balances were revised to ancient standards.

sentences.zh: 改上柱國以下官為大夫；

translations.literal: Offices from Superior Pillar of State downward were changed to grandees.
translations.idiomatic: Ranks from Superior Pillar of State down were retitled grandees.

sentences.zh: 置殿內省，與尚書、門下、內史、秘書為五省；

translations.literal: The Palace Secretariat was established, together with the Department of State Affairs, Chancellery, Palace Secretariat for Drafting, and Secretariat as the Five Departments.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Secretariat was added to form the Five Departments with the Department of State Affairs, Chancellery, Drafting Office, and Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 增謁者、司隸台，與御史為三台；

translations.literal: Attendants and the Metropolitan Inspectorate were added, together with the Censorate as the Three Platforms.
translations.idiomatic: The Attendants and Metropolitan Inspectorate joined the Censorate as the Three Platforms.

sentences.zh: 分太府寺置少府監，與長秋、國子、將作、都水為五監；

translations.literal: The Imperial Storehouse was split to establish the Lesser Treasury Directorate, together with the Long Autumn, Imperial University, Construction, and Waterways as the Five Directorates.
translations.idiomatic: The Lesser Treasury was split from the Imperial Storehouse to form the Five Directorates with Long Autumn, Imperial University, Construction, and Waterways.

sentences.zh: 又增改左、右翊衛等為十六府；

translations.literal: Left and Right Flank Guards and others were increased and changed to sixteen guard offices.
translations.idiomatic: The guard offices were expanded to sixteen, including the Left and Right Flank Guards.

sentences.zh: 廢伯、子、男爵，唯留王、公、侯三等。

translations.literal: Earl, viscount, and baron ranks were abolished; only the three ranks of king, duke, and marquis were retained.
translations.idiomatic: Earl, viscount, and baron were abolished, leaving only kings, dukes, and marquises.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，車駕北巡；

translations.literal: Day bingyin: the imperial carriage toured north.
translations.idiomatic: On day bingyin the emperor began a northern tour.

sentences.zh: 己亥，頓赤岸澤。

translations.literal: Day jihai: halted at Chian Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: On day jihai he halted at Chian Marsh.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁巳，突厥啟民可汗遣其子拓特勒來朝。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day dingsi: Qimin Khaghan of the Turks sent his son Tuotele to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on day dingsi, Qimin Khaghan sent his son Tuotele to court.

sentences.zh: 戊午，發河北十餘郡丁男鑿太行山，達於并州，以通馳道。

translations.literal: Day wuwu: adult males from more than ten Hebei commanderies were mobilized to cut through the Taihang Mountains as far as Bingzhou to open an imperial highway.
translations.idiomatic: On day wuwu corvée laborers from more than ten Hebei commanderies cut a highway through the Taihang Mountains to Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，啟民遣其兄子毘黎伽特勒來朝。

translations.literal: Day bingyin: Qimin sent his elder brother's son Pilijia Tegin to court.
translations.idiomatic: On day bingyin Qimin sent his nephew Pilijia Tegin to court.

sentences.zh: 辛未，啟民遣使請自入塞奉迎輿駕，上不許。

translations.literal: Day xinwei: Qimin sent envoys requesting to enter the passes himself to welcome the imperial carriage; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: On day xinwei Qimin asked to enter the passes to welcome the emperor in person; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖受禪，唯立四親廟，同殿異室而已。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gaozu received the abdication, he established only the temple of four progenitors, one hall with separate chambers.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne he built only the temple of the four progenitors in one hall with separate chambers.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，命有司議七廟之制。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne he ordered the offices to deliberate on the system of seven temples.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession he ordered officials to deliberate the system of seven ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎攝太常少卿許善心等奏請為太祖、高祖各立一殿，准周文、武二祧，與始祖而三，餘並分室而祭，從迭毀之法。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Xu Shansin, acting Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices, and others memorialized requesting separate halls for the Grand Progenitor and Gaozu, following the Zhou model of two distant ancestors with the founding ancestor as three, the rest in separate chambers with successive destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shansin, Vice Minister of Rites, and others proposed separate halls for the Grand Progenitor and Gaozu, following the Zhou two-ancestor model with the founder as three, the rest in side chambers under the law of successive removal.

sentences.zh: 至是，有司請如前議，於東京建宗廟。

translations.literal: At this time the offices requested as in the former proposal to build the ancestral temple at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The offices now asked to build the ancestral temple at the Eastern Capital as proposed.

sentences.zh: 帝謂秘書監柳辯曰：「今始祖及二祧已具，後世子孫處朕何所？」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Director of the Secretariat Liu Bian: "Now the founding ancestor and two distant ancestors are complete—where will later generations place me?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Secretariat Director Liu Bian, "The founder and two distant ancestors are provided for—where will my descendants place me?"

sentences.zh: 六月，丁亥，詔為高祖建別廟，仍修月祭禮。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day dinghai: an edict ordered a separate temple built for Gaozu and monthly sacrifice rites restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on day dinghai, an edict ordered a separate temple for Gaozu and the restoration of monthly sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 既而方事巡幸，竟不果立。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was occupied with tours and in the end it was not established.
translations.idiomatic: Tours intervened, and it was never built.

sentences.zh: 帝過雁門，雁門太守丘和獻食甚精；

translations.literal: The emperor passed Yanmen; Yanmen Governor Qiu He presented food of great refinement.
translations.idiomatic: At Yanmen, Governor Qiu He presented a lavish feast.

sentences.zh: 至馬邑，馬邑太守楊廓獨無所獻，帝不悅。

translations.literal: Reaching Mayi, Mayi Governor Yang Kuo alone presented nothing; the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: At Mayi, Governor Yang Kuo alone presented nothing, and the emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 以和為博陵太守，仍使廓至博陵觀和為式。

translations.literal: He was made governor of Boling, and Kuo was still sent to Boling to observe He's model.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu He was made governor of Boling, and Yang Kuo was sent there to learn from his example.

sentences.zh: 由是所至獻食，競為豐侈。

translations.literal: From this wherever he went food offerings competed in abundance and extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter every place he visited vied in extravagant feasts.

sentences.zh: 戊子，車駕頓榆林郡。

translations.literal: Day wuzi: the imperial carriage halted at Yulin Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On day wuzi the emperor halted at Yulin Commandery.

sentences.zh: 帝欲出塞耀兵，逕突厥中，指於涿郡，恐啟民驚懼，先遣武衛將軍長孫晟諭旨。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to leave the passes and display military might, passing through Turk lands toward Zhuo Commandery; fearing Qimin would be alarmed, he first sent Martial Guard General Zhangsun Sheng to explain the intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned to cross the frontier in force through Turk territory toward Zhuo Commandery; fearing Qimin would panic, he sent Zhangsun Sheng, Martial Guard General, ahead to explain.

sentences.zh: 啟民奉詔，因召所部諸國奚、□、室韋等酋長數十人咸集。

translations.literal: Qimin received the edict and thereupon summoned chiefs of the Xi, [character missing], Shiwei, and other peoples under his authority—several tens all gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Qimin obeyed and summoned dozens of chiefs of the Xi, Shiwei, and other subject peoples.

sentences.zh: 晟見牙帳中草穢，欲令啟民親除之，示諸部落，以明威重，乃指帳前草曰：「此根大香。」

translations.literal: Sheng saw the grass in the royal tent was filthy and wished Qimin to clear it personally to show the tribes and clarify majesty; he pointed to the grass before the tent and said: "This root is very fragrant."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng saw the royal tent overgrown with weeds and wanted Qimin to clear them himself as a lesson to the tribes; pointing at the grass he said, "This weed smells wonderful."

sentences.zh: 啟民遽嗅之，曰：「殊不香也。」

translations.literal: Qimin hastily sniffed it and said: "It is not fragrant at all."
translations.idiomatic: Qimin sniffed it and said, "It smells terrible."

sentences.zh: 晟曰：「天子行幸所在，諸侯躬自灑掃，耕除御路，以表至敬之心；

translations.literal: Sheng said: "Wherever the Son of Heaven tours, feudatory lords personally sprinkle and sweep and plow clear the imperial road to show utmost reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said, "Wherever the Son of Heaven travels, lords sweep the road themselves to show utmost respect.

sentences.zh: 今牙內蕪穢，謂是留香草耳！」

translations.literal: Now inside the tent it is overgrown and filthy—you call this leaving fragrant grass!"
translations.idiomatic: Your tent is filthy with weeds—is this how you show respect!"

sentences.zh: 啟民乃悟曰：「奴之罪也！

translations.literal: Qimin then understood and said: "This slave's crime!
translations.idiomatic: Qimin understood and cried, "Your slave has failed!

sentences.zh: 奴之骨肉皆天子所賜，得效筋力，豈敢有辭。

translations.literal: This slave's flesh and bone are all bestowed by the Son of Heaven; to offer sinew and strength—how dare there be refusal.
translations.idiomatic: My body and kin are the Son of Heaven's gift—I dare not refuse to serve.

sentences.zh: 特以邊人不知法耳，賴將軍教之；

translations.literal: It is only that border people do not know the law; relying on the general to teach them.
translations.idiomatic: We border folk know no better—thanks to the general for teaching us.

sentences.zh: 此將軍之惠，奴之幸也。」

translations.literal: This is the general's grace and the slave's fortune."
translations.idiomatic: This is the general's kindness and my good fortune."

sentences.zh: 遂拔所佩刀，自芟庭草。

translations.literal: Thereupon he drew the sword at his belt and himself cut the courtyard grass.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his sword and cut the courtyard weeds himself.

sentences.zh: 其貴人及諸部爭效之。

translations.literal: His nobles and all the tribes competed to imitate him.
translations.idiomatic: His nobles and all the tribes rushed to follow his example.

sentences.zh: 於是發榆林北境，至其牙，東達於薊，長三千里，廣百步，舉國就役，開為御道。

translations.literal: Thereupon from Yulin's northern border to his royal tent, east reaching Ji, three thousand li long and a hundred paces wide, the whole nation took corvée and opened an imperial road.
translations.idiomatic: From Yulin's northern border to his tent and east to Ji, three thousand li long and a hundred paces wide, the whole nation labored to build an imperial highway.

sentences.zh: 帝聞晟策，益嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of Sheng's stratagem and praised him still more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of Sheng's maneuver and praised him all the more.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，啟民及義成公主來朝行宮。

translations.literal: Day dingyou: Qimin and Princess Yicheng came to court at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: On day dingyou Qimin and Princess Yicheng attended the emperor at his traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 己亥，吐谷渾、高昌並遣使入貢。

translations.literal: Day jihai: Tuyuhun and Gaochang both sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On day jihai Tuyuhun and Gaochang both sent tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，上御北樓觀漁於河，以宴百僚。

translations.literal: Day jiachen: the emperor mounted the north tower to watch fishing on the river and feast the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: On day jiachen the emperor watched fishing from the north tower and feasted his officials.

sentences.zh: 定襄太守周法尚朝於行宮，太府卿元壽言於帝曰：「漢武出關，旌旗千里。

translations.literal: Dingxiang Governor Zhou Fashang attended at the traveling palace; Director of the Imperial Treasury Yuan Shou said to the emperor: "When Han Emperor Wu left the passes, banners and flags stretched a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxiang Governor Zhou Fashang attended court; Yuan Shou, Director of the Imperial Treasury, told the emperor, "When Han Emperor Wu left the passes, his banners stretched a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 今御營之外，請分為二十四軍，日別遣一軍發，相去三十里，旗幟相望，鉦鼓相聞，首尾相屬，千里不絕，此亦出師之盛者也。」

translations.literal: Outside the imperial camp now, I request division into twenty-four armies, each day sending one army forth, thirty li apart, banners and flags facing one another, gongs and drums heard by one another, head and tail linked, unbroken for a thousand li—this too is the grandeur of setting out on campaign."
translations.idiomatic: Let the camp outside be divided into twenty-four armies, one departing each day thirty li apart, banners and drums linking head to tail for a thousand li—that would match Han Wu's grandeur."

sentences.zh: 法尚曰：「不然，兵亙千里，動間山川，猝有不虞，四分五裂；

translations.literal: Fashang said: "Not so—troops stretching a thousand li, movement blocked by mountains and rivers, if suddenly there is the unexpected, they split four and five ways.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang objected, "No—an army stretched a thousand li is broken by terrain; at any surprise it shatters.

sentences.zh: 腹心有事，首尾未知，道路阻長，難以相救，雖有故事，乃取敗之道也。」

translations.literal: If the center has trouble, head and tail do not know; roads are long and obstructed and hard to rescue—though there is precedent, it is the way to defeat."
translations.idiomatic: If the center is struck, the ends cannot help; long roads prevent rescue. Precedent or not, that is the road to defeat."

sentences.zh: 帝不懌，曰：「卿意如何？」

translations.literal: The emperor was not pleased and said: "What is your idea?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and asked, "What do you propose?"

sentences.zh: 法尚曰：「結為方陳，四面外拒，六宮及百官家屬並在其內；

translations.literal: Fashang said: "Form a square array, resist outward on four sides, the six palaces and officials' families all within.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang said, "Form a square camp facing outward on all sides, with the palace women and officials' families inside.

sentences.zh: 若有變起，所當之面，即令抗拒，內引奇兵，出外奮擊，車為壁壘，重設鉤陳，此與據城，理亦何異！

translations.literal: If trouble arises, on whichever face it falls order resistance; inside lead picked troops outward to strike fiercely; chariots as ramparts, layered hook formations set again—how is this in principle different from holding a city!
translations.idiomatic: Whichever side is attacked, resist there; hold elite troops within to strike out; use wagons as walls in layered formations—it is no different from holding a city!

sentences.zh: 若戰而捷，抽騎追奔，萬一不捷，屯營自守，臣謂此萬全之策也。」

translations.literal: If battle is victorious, draw cavalry to pursue the fleeing; if by chance not victorious, encamp and hold—your servant considers this a ten-thousandfold safe plan."
translations.idiomatic: If we win, send cavalry in pursuit; if we lose, the camp holds itself. That is the sure plan."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Excellent!"

sentences.zh: 因拜法尚左武衛將軍。

translations.literal: He thereupon appointed Fashang Left Martial Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Fashang Left Martial Guard General.

sentences.zh: 啟民可汗復上表，以為「先帝可汗憐臣，賜臣安義公主，種種無乏。

translations.literal: Qimin Khaghan again submitted a memorial, stating that "the former emperor khaghan pitied your servant, bestowed Princess Anyi on your servant, and in every way there was no lack.
translations.idiomatic: Qimin Khaghan memorialized again: "The former emperor pitied me, gave me Princess Anyi, and provided everything I needed.

sentences.zh: 臣兄弟嫉妒，共欲殺臣。

translations.literal: Your servant's brothers were jealous and together wished to kill your servant.
translations.idiomatic: My brothers envied me and tried to kill me.

sentences.zh: 臣當是時，走無所適，仰視唯天，俯視唯地，奉身委命，依歸先帝。

translations.literal: Your servant at that time fled with nowhere to go, looking up only to Heaven, looking down only to earth, offering body and entrusting life, relying on and returning to the former emperor.
translations.idiomatic: I fled with nowhere to turn, looked only to Heaven and earth, and entrusted my life to the former emperor.

sentences.zh: 先帝憐臣且死，養而生之，以臣為大可汗，還撫突厥之民。

translations.literal: The former emperor pitied your servant near death, nurtured and revived him, made your servant great khaghan, and returned to pacify the Turk people.
translations.idiomatic: He pitied me near death, restored me, and made me great khaghan over the Turks.

sentences.zh: 至尊今御天下，還如先帝養生臣及突厥之民，種種無乏。

translations.literal: The Supreme One now rules all under Heaven and still, like the former emperor, nurtures your servant and the Turk people—in every way there is no lack.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty now rules the world and nurtures me and my people as the former emperor did, leaving us wanting nothing.

sentences.zh: 臣荷戴聖恩，言不能盡。

translations.literal: Your servant bears the sage grace; words cannot exhaust it.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot express my gratitude.

sentences.zh: 臣今非昔日突厥可汗，乃是至尊臣民，願帥部落變改衣服，一如華夏。」

translations.literal: Your servant today is not the Turk khaghan of former days but the Supreme One's subject; I wish to lead the tribes to change clothing to be like Huaxia."
translations.idiomatic: I am no longer the Turk khaghan but Your Majesty's subject; I wish to lead my tribes to dress like the Chinese."

sentences.zh: 帝以為不可。

translations.literal: The emperor considered it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛亥，賜啟民璽書，諭以「磧北未靜，猶須征戰，但存心恭順，何必變服？」

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day xinhai: he bestowed an imperial-seal letter on Qimin, instructing him that "north of the deserts is not yet calm and campaigns are still needed—only keep your heart respectful and obedient; why must you change dress?"
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on day xinhai, he sent Qimin an imperial letter: "The north is not yet pacified and war continues—stay obedient in heart; why change your dress?"

sentences.zh: 帝欲誇示突厥，令宇文愷為大帳，其下可坐數千人；

translations.literal: The emperor wished to display grandeur to the Turks and ordered Yuwen Kai to make a great tent under which several thousand could sit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to impress the Turks and had Yuwen Kai build a great tent seating thousands.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，帝於城東御大帳，備儀衛，宴啟民及其部落，作散樂。

translations.literal: Day jiayin: the emperor at the great tent east of the city, with full guards and escort, feasted Qimin and his tribes and performed scattered music.
translations.idiomatic: On day jiayin he feasted Qimin and his tribes in the great tent east of the city with full ceremony and scattered entertainments.

sentences.zh: 諸胡駭悅，爭獻牛羊駝馬數千萬頭。

translations.literal: The various Hu were amazed and pleased and competed to present cattle, sheep, camels, and horses numbering tens of millions of head.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier peoples were awed and delighted, competing to offer tens of millions of cattle, sheep, camels, and horses.

sentences.zh: 帝賜啟民帛二千萬段，其下各有差。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed on Qimin twenty million bolts of silk; those below each received differing amounts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave Qimin twenty million bolts of silk and lesser gifts to his followers.

sentences.zh: 又賜啟民路車乘馬，鼓歡幡旗，贊拜不名，位在諸侯王上。

translations.literal: He also bestowed on Qimin a state carriage and riding horses, drums, banners, and flags of rejoicing; in laudatory address his name was not spoken, and his position was above feudatory princes.
translations.idiomatic: He also gave Qimin an imperial carriage, horses, drums and banners, the honor of not having his name spoken in audience, and rank above the feudatory princes.

sentences.zh: 又詔發丁男百餘萬築長城，西拒榆林，東至紫河。

translations.literal: An edict also mobilized more than a million adult males to build the Long Wall from Yulin in the west to the Zi River in the east.
translations.idiomatic: An edict mobilized more than a million men to build the Great Wall from Yulin west to the Zi River east.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射蘇威諫，帝不聽，築之二旬而畢。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Su Wei remonstrated; the emperor did not listen, and construction was completed in twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei, Left Vice Director, remonstrated in vain; the wall was finished in twenty days.

sentences.zh: 帝之征散樂也，太常卿高熲諫，不聽。

translations.literal: When the emperor recruited scattered music, Director of Imperial Sacrifices Gao Feng remonstrated; he did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor recruited scattered entertainers, Gao Feng, Director of Imperial Sacrifices, remonstrated in vain.

sentences.zh: 熲退，謂太常丞李懿曰：「周天元以好樂而亡，殷鑒不遠，安可復爾！」

translations.literal: Feng withdrew and said to Imperial Sacrifices Aide Li Yi: "Northern Zhou Emperor Xuan died through love of music—the warning mirror is not far; how can we do this again!"
translations.idiomatic: Feng told Imperial Sacrifices Aide Li Yi, "Northern Zhou's Emperor Xuan destroyed his state with music—the lesson is recent; how can we repeat it!"

sentences.zh: 熲又以帝遇啟民過厚，謂太府卿何稠曰：「此虜頗知中國虛實，山川險易，恐為後患。」

translations.literal: Feng also, because the emperor treated Qimin too generously, said to Director of the Imperial Treasury He Chou: "This barbarian knows rather well the emptiness and fullness of China, the ease and difficulty of mountains and rivers— I fear a later trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Feng also told He Chou, Director of the Imperial Treasury, "This barbarian now knows China's strengths and terrain—he may become a future threat."

sentences.zh: 又謂觀王雄曰：「近來朝廷殊無綱紀。」

translations.literal: He also said to Prince Guan Xiong: "Recently the court altogether lacks discipline."
translations.idiomatic: He told Prince Guan Xiong, "The court lately has no discipline at all."

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書宇文弼私謂熲曰：「天元之侈，以今方之，不亦甚乎？」

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Yuwen Bi privately said to Feng: "Emperor Xuan's extravagance—compared with today, is it not still greater?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Bi, Minister of Rites, whispered to Feng, "Compared with Emperor Xuan, is today's extravagance not worse?"

sentences.zh: 又言：「長城之役，幸非急務。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The Long Wall labor—fortunately it is not urgent business."
translations.idiomatic: He also said the Great Wall project was no urgent necessity.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫賀若弼亦私議宴可汗太侈。

translations.literal: Household Counsellor He Ruo Bi also privately discussed that the feast for the khaghan was too extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruo Bi, Household Counsellor, also privately said the feast for the khaghan was too lavish.

sentences.zh: 並為人所奏。

translations.literal: All were reported by others.
translations.idiomatic: All were reported to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝以為誹謗朝政，丙子，高熲、宇文弼、賀若弼皆坐誅，熲諸子徙邊，弼妻子沒官為奴婢。

translations.literal: The emperor considered it slander of court government; on day bingzi Gao Feng, Yuwen Bi, and He Ruo Bi were all punished with execution; Feng's sons were exiled to the frontier; Bi's wife and children were confiscated as government slaves.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deemed it slander of the government; on day bingzi Gao Feng, Yuwen Bi, and He Ruo Bi were executed; Feng's sons were exiled and Bi's family enslaved.

sentences.zh: 事連蘇威，亦坐免官。

translations.literal: The affair implicated Su Wei, who was also punished by dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei was implicated and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 熲有文武大略，明達世務，自蒙寄任，竭誠盡節，進引貞良，以天下為己任；

translations.literal: Feng had civil and military great strategy, was clear and penetrating in worldly affairs; from receiving entrustment he exhausted loyalty and utmost integrity, advanced and introduced the upright and good, and took all under Heaven as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: Feng had great civil and military talent, served with complete loyalty, promoted worthy men, and took the empire as his charge.

sentences.zh: 蘇威、楊素、賀若弼、韓擒虎皆熲所推薦，自餘立功立事者不可勝數；

translations.literal: Su Wei, Yang Su, He Ruo Bi, and Han Qinhu were all recommended by Feng; besides these, those who established merit and achievement were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei, Yang Su, He Ruo Bi, and Han Qinhu were all his protégés; countless others owed their success to him.

sentences.zh: 當朝執政將二十年，朝野推服，物無異議，海內富庶，熲之力也。

translations.literal: He governed the court for nearly twenty years; court and countryside deferred to him, the world had no differing opinions, and wealth within the seas was his power's doing.
translations.idiomatic: He dominated the court for nearly twenty years; the empire prospered through his efforts, and none disputed his authority.

sentences.zh: 及死，天下莫不傷之。

translations.literal: When he died, none under Heaven did not grieve.
translations.idiomatic: When he died the empire grieved.

sentences.zh: 先是，蕭琮以皇后故，甚見親重，為內史令，改封梁公，宗族緦麻以上，皆隨才擢用，諸蕭昆弟，布列朝廷。

translations.literal: Earlier Xiao Cong, because of the empress, was greatly favored and esteemed, made Drafting Director, changed enfeoffment to Duke of Liang; kinsmen of mourning-grade fine hemp and above were all promoted according to talent; the Xiao brothers were arrayed throughout the court.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xiao Cong, the empress's kinsman, had been favored as Drafting Director and Duke of Liang; Xiao clansmen filled the court.

sentences.zh: 琮性澹雅，不以職務為意，身雖羈旅，見北間豪貴，無所降下。

translations.literal: Cong's nature was tranquil and refined; he did not take official duties to heart; though himself a sojourner, facing northern magnates and nobles he bowed to none.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was refined and indifferent to office; though a captive prince, he bowed to no northern grandee.

sentences.zh: 與賀若弼善，弼既誅，又有童謠曰：「蕭蕭亦復起。」

translations.literal: He was friendly with He Ruo Bi; after Bi was executed there was also a children's song: "Xiao Xiao will rise again."
translations.idiomatic: He was close to He Ruo Bi; after Bi's execution a children's song ran, "Xiao Xiao will rise again."

sentences.zh: 帝由是忌之，遂廢於家，未幾而卒。

translations.literal: "The emperor therefore resented him, thereupon dismissed him to his home, and before long he died."
translations.idiomatic: "The emperor grew suspicious, confined him at home, and he soon died."

sentences.zh: 八月，壬午，車駕發榆林，歷雲中，溯金河。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day renwu: the imperial carriage departed Yulin, passed through Yunzhong, and went up the Golden River.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on day renwu, the emperor left Yulin, passed Yunzhong, and ascended the Golden River.

sentences.zh: 時天下承平，百物豐實，甲士五十餘萬，馬十萬匹，旌旗輜重，千里不絕。

translations.literal: At that time the empire was at peace, all things abundant and full; armored soldiers numbered more than five hundred thousand, horses one hundred thousand; banners, flags, and baggage trains were unbroken for a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was at peace and abundance; more than five hundred thousand armored men and a hundred thousand horses marched with banners and baggage stretching unbroken for a thousand li.
