sentences.zh: 令宇文愷等造觀風行殿，上容侍衛者數百人，離合為之，下施輪軸，倏忽推移。

translations.literal: Yuwen Kai and others were ordered to make a Wind-Viewing Traveling Hall holding several hundred attendants and guards, joined and separated as needed, with wheels and axles below, shifting in an instant.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Kai built a Wind-Viewing Traveling Hall for hundreds of guards, mounted on wheels so it could move in an instant.

sentences.zh: 又作行城，週二千步，以板為干，衣之以布，飾以丹青，樓櫓悉備。

translations.literal: A traveling city was also made, two thousand paces in circuit, with boards as shields, clothed in cloth, adorned with cinnabar and green, towers and watchtowers all complete.
translations.idiomatic: They also built a traveling fort two thousand paces around, with board shields draped in cloth and painted, complete with towers.

sentences.zh: 胡人驚以為神，每望御營，十里之外，屈膝稽顙，無敢乘馬。

translations.literal: The Hu were amazed and considered it divine; whenever they gazed at the imperial camp, beyond ten li they knelt and touched their foreheads to the ground, none daring to ride horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu thought it divine; ten li from the imperial camp they knelt and touched their foreheads to the ground, none daring to ride.

sentences.zh: 啟民奉廬帳以俟車駕。

translations.literal: Qimin presented a felt tent to await the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Qimin pitched his felt tent to await the emperor.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，帝幸其帳，啟民奉觴上壽，跪伏恭甚，王侯以下袒割於帳前，莫敢仰視。

translations.literal: Day yiyou: the emperor visited his tent; Qimin presented a cup and offered longevity wishes, kneeling and prostrate with great respect; princes and marquises down bared their shoulders and cut meat before the tent, none daring to look up.
translations.idiomatic: On day yiyou the emperor visited his tent; Qimin offered wine and wishes for long life, kneeling in deepest respect; nobles down to marquises bared their shoulders and carved meat before the tent, none daring to look up.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賦詩曰：「呼韓頓顙至，屠耆接踵來；

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and composed a poem: "Huhhan touches forehead and comes, Tujue follows in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and composed a poem: "Huhhan comes bowing, Tujue follows in turn;

sentences.zh: 何如漢天子，空上單于台。」

translations.literal: How does this compare with the Han Son of Heaven, vainly mounting the Single Leader's terrace?"
translations.idiomatic: how unlike the Han emperor who vainly climbed the Chanyu's terrace."

sentences.zh: 皇后亦幸義成公主帳。

translations.literal: The empress also visited Princess Yicheng's tent.
translations.idiomatic: The empress also visited Princess Yicheng's tent.

sentences.zh: 帝賜啟民及公主金甕各一，並衣服被褥錦彩，特勒以下，受賜各有差。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed on Qimin and the princess each one golden urn, together with clothing, bedding, and brocades; from tegin downward, gifts differed in degree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave Qimin and the princess each a golden urn, clothing, bedding, and brocades; lesser ranks received gifts in proportion.

sentences.zh: 帝還，啟民從入塞，己丑，遣歸國。

translations.literal: The emperor returned; Qimin followed into the passes; on day jichou he was sent back to his state.
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey Qimin followed into the passes; on day jichou he was sent home.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，入樓煩關；

translations.literal: Day guisi: entered Loufan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On day guisi he entered Loufan Pass.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，至太原，詔營晉陽宮。

translations.literal: Day renyin: reached Taiyuan; an edict ordered construction of the Jinyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On day renyin he reached Taiyuan and ordered the Jinyang Palace built.

sentences.zh: 帝謂御史大夫張衡曰：「朕欲過公宅，可為朕作主人。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Censor-in-Chief Zhang Heng: "I wish to pass by your residence—you may act as host for me."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Censor-in-Chief Zhang Heng, "I mean to visit your home—be my host."

sentences.zh: 衡乃先馳至河內，具牛酒。

translations.literal: Heng thereupon galloped ahead to Henei and prepared cattle and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Heng rode ahead to Henei and prepared beef and wine.

sentences.zh: 帝上太行，開直道九十里，九月，己未，至濟源，幸衡宅。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended the Taihang, opened a straight road ninety li, and in the ninth month on day jiwei reached Jiyuan and visited Heng's residence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor crossed the Taihang, cut a straight road ninety li long, and in the ninth month, on day jiwei, reached Jiyuan and visited Heng's home.

sentences.zh: 帝悅其山泉，留宴三日，賜賚甚厚。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased with its mountain springs, remained feasting three days, and bestowed gifts very generously.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in the mountain springs, stayed three days feasting, and gave lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 衡復獻食，帝令頒賜公卿，下至衛士，無不沾洽。

translations.literal: Heng again presented food; the emperor ordered it distributed to the dukes and ministers down to the guards—none went without a share.
translations.idiomatic: Heng presented more food, and the emperor had it distributed from the highest ministers down to the guards until everyone had a share.

sentences.zh: 己巳，至東都。

translations.literal: Day jisi: reached the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On day jisi he reached the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 壬申，以齊王暕為河南尹；

translations.literal: Day renshen: Prince of Qi Yang Jian was made Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: On day renshen Prince of Qi Yang Jian was made Governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，以民部尚書楊文思為納言。

translations.literal: Day guiyou: Minister of the People Yang Wensi was made Palace Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: On day guiyou Yang Wensi, Minister of the People, was made Palace Counselor.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，敕河北諸郡送一藝戶陪東都三千餘家，置十二坊於洛水南以處之。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: an edict ordered the commanderies of Hebei to send households of one craft each to accompany more than three thousand families to the Eastern Capital, establishing twelve wards south of the Luo River to house them.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Hebei commanderies were ordered to send artisan households—more than three thousand families in all—to the Eastern Capital, housed in twelve wards south of the Luo River.

sentences.zh: 西域諸胡多至張掖交市，帝使吏部侍郎裴矩掌之。

translations.literal: The various Hu of the Western Regions mostly came to Zhangye to trade; the emperor had Vice Minister of Personnel Pei Ju oversee it.
translations.idiomatic: Many Western Region peoples traded at Zhangye; the emperor put Vice Minister of Personnel Pei Ju in charge.

sentences.zh: 矩知帝好遠略，諸商胡至者，矩誘訪諸國山川風俗，王及庶人儀形服飾，撰《西域圖記》三卷，合四十四國，入朝奏之。

translations.literal: Ju knew the emperor loved far-reaching strategy; for merchant Hu who arrived he drew out inquiries on each state's mountains, rivers, customs, the forms and dress of kings and commoners, and compiled three juan of Records of the Western Regions, forty-four states in all, entering court to memorialize it.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the emperor's appetite for conquest, Ju questioned every merchant about the mountains, customs, and dress of forty-four states and compiled three juan of Records of the Western Regions, which he presented at court.

sentences.zh: 仍別造地圖，窮其要害，從西傾以去，縱橫所亙，將二萬里，發自敦煌，至於西海，凡為三道，北道從伊吾，中道從高昌，南道從鄯善，總湊敦煌。

translations.literal: He also separately made maps, exhausting their key points; from Mount Xiqing westward, the span east-west and north-south was nearly twenty thousand li, starting from Dunhuang to the Western Sea—in all three routes: the northern route from Yiwu, the central from Gaochang, the southern from Shanshan, all converging at Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He also drew maps of the key routes west from Mount Xiqing—nearly twenty thousand li from Dunhuang to the Western Sea—three roads north through Yiwu, center through Gaochang, and south through Shanshan, all meeting at Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 且云：「以國家威德，將士驍雄，泛濛汜而越崑崙，易如反掌。

translations.literal: Moreover he said: "With the state's majesty and virtue, officers and soldiers fierce and heroic, to sail the Mengsi and cross Kunlun is easy as turning the palm.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "With the empire's might and our brave troops, crossing the Mengsi and Kunlun would be as easy as turning one's hand.

sentences.zh: 但突厥、吐渾分領羌、胡之國，為其壅遏，故朝貢不通。

translations.literal: Only the Turks and Tuyuhun divide rule over the Qiang and Hu states and block them, so tribute missions do not pass.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Turks and Tuyuhun, controlling the Qiang and Hu peoples, block the way, so tribute does not reach us.

sentences.zh: 今並因商人密送誠款，引領翹首，願為臣妾。

translations.literal: Now all through merchants secretly send sincere pledges, leading and craning their necks, wishing to become subjects and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Now through merchants they secretly send loyalty and crane their necks in hope, wishing to become our subjects.

sentences.zh: 若服而撫之，務存安輯，皇華遣使，弗動兵車，諸蕃既從，渾、厥可滅，混壹戎、夏，其在茲乎！」

translations.literal: If they submit and are pacified, striving to preserve peace and order, imperial envoys are sent and war chariots are not moved—once the various barbarians follow, Tuyuhun and the Turks can be destroyed, and unifying barbarian and Chinese is in this!"
translations.idiomatic: If we win them by kindness and send envoys without war chariots, once the frontier peoples submit, Tuyuhun and the Turks can be destroyed and barbarian and Chinese unified—this is the moment!"

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賜帛五百段，日引矩至御坐，親問西域事。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, bestowed five hundred bolts of silk, and daily summoned Ju to the imperial seat to question him personally on Western Region affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, gave him five hundred bolts of silk, and daily summoned him to question him about the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 矩盛言「胡中多諸珍寶，吐谷渾易可併吞。」

translations.literal: Ju spoke at length that "among the Hu are many rare treasures, and Tuyuhun can easily be swallowed whole."
translations.idiomatic: Ju stressed that "the frontier holds many treasures and Tuyuhun can easily be swallowed whole."

sentences.zh: 帝於是慨然慕秦皇、漢武之功，甘心將通西域；

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon sighed with longing for the achievements of Qin Emperor Huang and Han Emperor Wu, willing in heart to open the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed with longing for the deeds of the First Emperor and Han Wudi and set his heart on opening the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 四夷經略，鹹以委之。

translations.literal: Strategy toward the four barbarians was all entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: All frontier strategy was entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 以矩為黃門侍郎，復使至張掖，引致諸胡，啗之以利，勸令入朝。

translations.literal: Ju was made Yellow Gate Attendant and again sent to Zhangye to draw in the various Hu, baiting them with profit and urging them to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Ju was made Yellow Gate Attendant and sent again to Zhangye to lure the frontier peoples with profit and urge them to court.

sentences.zh: 自是西域諸胡往來相繼，所經郡縣，疲於送迎，糜費以萬萬計，卒令中國疲弊以至於亡，皆矩之唱導也。

translations.literal: From this the various Hu of the Western Regions came and went in succession; every commandery and county they passed was exhausted by sending them off and receiving them, waste calculated in tens of millions, and in the end China was worn out to the point of perishing—all was Ju's initiating guidance.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Western Region peoples came and went in endless streams; every commandery and county was exhausted hosting them at a cost of tens of millions, until China was drained to ruin—all Ju's doing.

sentences.zh: 鐵勒寇邊，帝遣將軍馮孝慈出敦煌擊之，不利。

translations.literal: The Tiele raided the frontier; the emperor sent General Feng Xiaoci out from Dunhuang to strike them, with unfavorable result.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele raided the frontier; the emperor sent General Feng Xiaoci from Dunhuang against them, without success.

sentences.zh: 鐵勒尋遣使謝罪，請降；

translations.literal: The Tiele soon sent envoys to apologize for their crime and request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele soon sent envoys to apologize and surrender.

sentences.zh: 帝使裴矩慰撫之。

translations.literal: The emperor had Pei Ju console and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Pei Ju to console and accept them.
